  • ✅ Profiling and benchmarking guide
  • ✅ Platform-specific optimization notes
  • ✅ Common pitfalls and solutions
  • ✅ Complete API documentation
  • ✅ Production-ready optimization checklist

Implementation Summary

This Zig implementation provides full feature parity with the Go reference implementation:

  • 14 Phases completed over comprehensive development cycle
  • 200+ test cases across unit, integration, and property-based tests
  • Minimal dependencies -- only thread-pool (optional, for parallelism; enabled by default, disable with -Dthread_pool=false)
  • Memory safe with explicit allocator management
  • Thread-safe graph operations where needed
  • Deterministic output for all algorithms
  • Performance optimized with detailed tuning guide

Quick Start

# Build the library
zig build

# Run tests
zig build test

# Run benchmarks
zig build bench

Requirements

  • Zig 0.16.0 or later

Core Design Principles

  1. Deterministic output - Stable, reproducible results
  2. Type safety - Compile-time generics with Zig's type system
  3. Memory safety - Explicit allocators, no hidden allocations
  4. Performance - Zero-cost abstractions where possible
  5. Concurrency - Mutex-protected Graph mutations; basic data structures (Stack, Queue, Deque) require external synchronization
  6. Error handling - Explicit error sets, no panics for user errors

API Examples

Stack

const std = @import("std");
const ds = @import("ds");

var stack = ds.Stack(i32).init(allocator);
defer stack.deinit();

try stack.push(1);
try stack.push(2);
const value = stack.pop(); // Returns ?i32

Queue

var queue = ds.Queue(i32).init(allocator);
defer queue.deinit();

try queue.enqueue(1);
try queue.enqueue(2);
const value = queue.dequeue(); // Returns ?i32

Deque

var deque = try ds.Deque(i32).init(allocator, 16);
defer deque.deinit();

try deque.pushBack(1);
try deque.pushFront(0);
const front = deque.popFront();
const back = deque.popBack();

Set

var set = ds.Set(i32).init(allocator);
defer set.deinit();

try set.add(1);
try set.add(2);
const has = set.contains(1); // Returns bool

BST

const Order = std.math.Order;
fn compareI32(a: i32, b: i32) Order {
    if (a < b) return .lt;
    if (a > b) return .gt;
    return .eq;
}

var bst = ds.BST(i32).init(allocator, compareI32);
defer bst.deinit();

try bst.insert(5);
try bst.insert(3);
const value = bst.search(5); // Returns ?i32

RBTree

var tree = ds.RBTree(i32).init(allocator, compareI32);
defer tree.deinit();

try tree.insert(5);
_ = tree.delete(5); // Returns bool

SkipList

var list = try ds.SkipList(i32, []const u8).init(allocator, 42, compareI32);
defer list.deinit();

try list.insert(5, "five");
const value = list.search(5); // Returns ?[]const u8
_ = try list.delete(5); // Returns Allocator.Error!bool

Trie

var trie = try ds.Trie.init(allocator);
defer trie.deinit();

try trie.insert("cat", 1);
const value = trie.search("cat"); // Returns ?usize
const has_prefix = trie.startsWith("ca"); // Returns bool

Graph

var graph = ds.Graph(i32).init(allocator);
defer graph.deinit();

// Create vertices
var v1 = try ds.Vertex(i32).initWithId(allocator, "A", 1);
var v2 = try ds.Vertex(i32).initWithId(allocator, "B", 2);

graph.addVertex(v1);
graph.addVertex(v2);

// Create a directed, weighted edge
var edge = try ds.createEdge(i32, allocator, v1, v2, 10, .{
    .directed = true,
    .weighted = true,
    .weight = 5.0,
});

graph.addEdge(edge);

// Query graph properties
const is_directed = graph.isDirected(); // true
const is_weighted = graph.isWeighted(); // true
const version = graph.getVersion(); // Mutation counter

// Find vertices
const found = graph.findVertexById("A"); // Returns ?*Vertex(i32)

Graph Algorithms

// BFS - Breadth-First Search
var bfs_result = try ds.bfsFrom(i32, &graph, v1, allocator);
defer bfs_result.deinit();
// bfs_result.order contains visit order
// bfs_result.prev contains predecessor map

// DFS - Depth-First Search (iterative)
var dfs_result = try ds.dfsFrom(i32, &graph, v1, allocator);
defer dfs_result.deinit();

// Topological Sort (Kahn's algorithm)
var topo = try ds.topoKahn(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer topo.deinit();
if (topo.is_acyclic) {
    // topo.order contains topologically sorted vertices
}

// Topological Sort (DFS-based)
var topo_dfs = try ds.topoDFS(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer topo_dfs.deinit();

// Cycle Detection
const has_cycle_directed = try ds.cycleDetectDirected(i32, &graph, allocator);
const has_cycle_undirected = try ds.cycleDetectUndirected(i32, &graph, allocator);

// Multi-source BFS
const sources = [_]*ds.Vertex(i32){ v1, v2 };
var distances = try ds.multiSourceBFS(i32, &graph, &sources, allocator);
defer distances.deinit();
// distances maps vertex IDs to shortest distance from any source

Shortest Path Algorithms

// Dijkstra's algorithm - shortest path in weighted graphs
var path = try ds.dijkstra(i32, &graph, v1, v3, allocator);
defer path.deinit();
if (!path.isEmpty()) {
    // path.nodes contains vertex IDs in order
    // path.cost contains total path cost
}

// A* pathfinding - with heuristic function
fn euclideanHeuristic(a: *ds.Vertex(anyopaque), b: *ds.Vertex(anyopaque)) f64 {
    // Return estimated distance from a to b
    return 0.0;
}
var path_astar = try ds.aStar(i32, &graph, v1, v3, euclideanHeuristic, allocator);
defer path_astar.deinit();

// IDDFS - Iterative Deepening Depth-First Search
var path_iddfs = try ds.iddfs(i32, &graph, v1, "C", 10, allocator);
defer path_iddfs.deinit();

// DAG Shortest Path - for directed acyclic graphs (more efficient than Dijkstra)
var path_dag = try ds.dagShortestPath(i32, &graph, v1, v2, allocator);
defer path_dag.deinit();

Connectivity & Spanning Trees

// Strongly Connected Components (Tarjan's algorithm)
var scc_result = try ds.sccTarjan(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer scc_result.deinit();
// scc_result.components contains strongly connected components
// Each component is sorted lexicographically

// Articulation Points and Bridges
var ab_result = try ds.articulationBridges(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer ab_result.deinit();
// ab_result.points contains articulation points (critical vertices)
// ab_result.bridges contains bridges (critical edges)

// Minimum Spanning Tree - Kruskal's algorithm
var mst_kruskal = try ds.kruskal(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer mst_kruskal.deinit();
// mst_kruskal.edges contains MST edges
// mst_kruskal.total_weight contains total MST weight

// Minimum Spanning Tree - Prim's algorithm
var mst_prim = try ds.prim(i32, &graph, start_vertex, allocator);
defer mst_prim.deinit();

// Union-Find data structure
var uf = ds.UnionFind.init(allocator);
defer uf.deinit();

try uf.make("A");
try uf.make("B");
const merged = try uf.unite("A", "B"); // true if sets were merged
const root = try uf.find("A"); // find representative
const set_size = try uf.size("A"); // size of set containing A

Flow & Matching Algorithms

// Maximum Flow - Edmonds-Karp algorithm
var flow_result = try ds.edmondsKarp(i32, &graph, source, sink, allocator);
defer flow_result.deinit();
// flow_result.flow contains maximum flow value
// flow_result.residual contains residual capacities

// Maximum Flow - Dinic's algorithm (faster for dense graphs)
var dinic_result = try ds.dinic(i32, &graph, source, sink, allocator);
defer dinic_result.deinit();

// Bipartite Matching - Hopcroft-Karp algorithm
const U = [_]*ds.Vertex(i32){ u1, u2, u3 }; // Left partition
const V = [_]*ds.Vertex(i32){ v1, v2, v3 }; // Right partition
var matching_result = try ds.hopcroftKarp(i32, &graph, &U, &V, allocator);
defer matching_result.deinit();
// matching_result.size contains matching size
// matching_result.matching maps vertices in U to V

Centrality & Metrics

// PageRank - power iteration algorithm
var pr_result = try ds.pageRank(i32, &graph, 0.85, 1e-8, 100, allocator);
defer pr_result.deinit();
// pr_result.scores contains PageRank scores for each vertex
// pr_result.iterations shows convergence iterations

// Betweenness and Closeness Centrality - Brandes algorithm
var cent_result = try ds.computeCentrality(i32, &graph, allocator);
defer cent_result.deinit();
// cent_result.betweenness contains betweenness centrality scores
// cent_result.closeness contains closeness centrality scores

Caching & Probabilistic Structures

// LRU Cache - Least Recently Used eviction
var lru = ds.LRU(i32, []const u8).init(allocator, 100);
defer lru.deinit();

try lru.put(1, "one");
try lru.put(2, "two");
if (try lru.get(1)) |value| {
    // Retrieved value, also marks as recently used
}

// LFU Cache - Least Frequently Used eviction
var lfu = ds.LFU(i32, []const u8).init(allocator, 100);
defer lfu.deinit();

try lfu.put(1, "one");
if (try lfu.get(1)) |value| {
    // Retrieved value, increases frequency counter
}

// Bloom Filter - Probabilistic set membership
var bloom = try ds.BloomFilter.init(allocator, 1000, 0.01, 42);
defer bloom.deinit();

bloom.add("key1");
bloom.add("key2");
if (bloom.mightContain("key1")) {
    // Likely in set (no false negatives)
}

String Search Algorithms

const text = "hello world, hello universe";
const pattern = "hello";

// KMP - Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm
const kmp_matches = try ds.findAllKMP(allocator, text, pattern);
defer allocator.free(kmp_matches);
// kmp_matches contains [0, 13] - indices where "hello" starts

// Rabin-Karp - rolling hash algorithm
const rk_matches = try ds.findAllRabinKarp(allocator, text, pattern);
defer allocator.free(rk_matches);
// rk_matches contains [0, 13] - same results as KMP

// Both algorithms:
// - Find all occurrences of pattern in text
// - Return starting indices of matches
// - Handle overlapping patterns correctly
// - O(n+m) average time complexity

DOT Format Support

// Parse a DOT format graph
const dot_input = "graph { \"A\" -- \"B\" -- \"C\" }";
var stream = std.io.fixedBufferStream(dot_input);

var dot_graph = try ds.DOTGraph.unmarshal(allocator, stream.reader());
defer {
    dot_graph.graph.deinit();
    allocator.destroy(dot_graph.graph);
    dot_graph.deinit();
}

// Access the parsed graph
const vertices = dot_graph.graph.vertices.items;  // 3 vertices
const edges = dot_graph.graph.edges.items;        // 2 edges

// Serialize a graph to DOT format
var my_graph = ds.Graph([]const u8).init(allocator);
defer my_graph.deinit();

// ... add vertices and edges ...

var dot = try ds.DOTGraph.init(allocator, &my_graph);
defer dot.deinit();

var output = std.ArrayList(u8).init(allocator);
defer output.deinit();

try dot.marshal(output.writer());
// output contains canonical DOT format

// Features:
// - Parse and serialize graph/digraph
// - Node and edge attributes
// - Strict mode (deduplication)
// - Canonical ordering for reproducible output
// - Roundtrip compatibility

GQL Emission

// Build a graph
var graph = ds.Graph([]const u8).init(allocator);
defer graph.deinit();

// ... add vertices and edges ...

// Emit CREATE clauses for ISO-GQL
var create_result = try ds.emitCreateGQL([]const u8, &graph, allocator);
defer create_result.deinit();

// Query string with parameterized node creation
// CREATE (nA:Node {id: $nid_A}), (nB:Node {id: $nid_B})
// CREATE (nA)-[:REL]->(nB)
const query = create_result.query;

// Parameters for safe query execution
// {"nid_A": "A", "nid_B": "B"}
var params_iter = create_result.params.iterator();
while (params_iter.next()) |entry| {
    const param_name = entry.key_ptr.*;
    const param_value = entry.value_ptr.*;
    // Use with your GQL database driver
}

// Emit MATCH query for shortest path
var match_result = try ds.emitMatchShortestPathGQL("A", "C", allocator);
defer match_result.deinit();

// MATCH (s:Node {id: $sid}), (t:Node {id: $tid}),
//       p = shortestPath((s)-[:REL*..]->(t)) RETURN p
const shortest_path_query = match_result.query;

// Parameters: {"sid": "A", "tid": "C"}
const start_id = match_result.params.get("sid").?;
const end_id = match_result.params.get("tid").?;

// Features:
// - ISO-GQL flavored CREATE clauses
// - Parameterized queries for SQL injection safety
// - Deterministic vertex/edge ordering
// - ID sanitization for safe aliases
// - Support for directed and undirected graphs
// - MATCH queries for shortest path patterns

Performance & Optimization

For detailed performance tuning, profiling, and optimization strategies, see PERFORMANCE.md.

Key topics covered:

  • Memory management and allocator selection
  • Algorithm selection guidelines
  • Caching strategies (LRU vs LFU)
  • Bloom filter tuning
  • Profiling and benchmarking
  • Platform-specific optimizations
  • Common performance pitfalls

Quick Performance Tips

// ✅ Pre-allocate capacity when size is known
try graph.vertices.ensureTotalCapacity(expected_count);

// ✅ Use ArenaAllocator for short-lived graphs
var arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(std.heap.page_allocator);
defer arena.deinit();

// ✅ Cache vertex lookups in a map
var vertex_map = std.AutoHashMap([]const u8, *Vertex(T)).init(allocator);

// ✅ Choose the right algorithm for your graph
const path = if (graph.isWeighted())
    try ds.dijkstra(graph, start, end, allocator)
else
    try ds.bfsFrom(graph, start, allocator);

Testing

The library includes comprehensive test coverage:

  • Unit tests: Individual component testing
  • Integration tests: Multi-component workflows
  • Property-based tests: Mathematical invariant verification
  • 200+ test cases across all modules

Run tests:

zig build test

Documentation

  • README.md: This file - overview and examples
  • PERFORMANCE.md: Detailed performance tuning guide
  • Source code: Comprehensive inline documentation
  • Test files: Examples of all functionality

Architecture

The library is organized into logical modules:

zig/src/
├── ds.zig                    # Main module exports
├── graph_core.zig            # Vertex, Edge definitions
├── graph.zig                 # Graph structure
├── graph_algorithms.zig      # BFS, DFS, topo sort, cycles
├── shortest_paths.zig        # Dijkstra, A*, IDDFS, DAG SP
├── connectivity.zig          # SCC, articulation, bridges
├── spanning_trees.zig        # MST (Kruskal, Prim)
├── unionfind.zig            # Union-Find with path compression
├── flow.zig                  # Edmonds-Karp, Dinic
├── matching.zig              # Hopcroft-Karp bipartite matching
├── centrality.zig            # PageRank, betweenness, closeness
├── cache.zig                 # LRU, LFU, Bloom filter
├── string_search.zig         # KMP, Rabin-Karp, Boyer-Moore
├── all_pairs_paths.zig       # Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall
├── parallel.zig              # Flat-chunking parallel utilities (thread-pool)
├── stack.zig                 # Generic LIFO stack
├── dot.zig                   # DOT format parser/serializer
├── gql.zig                   # GQL query emission
└── property_test.zig         # Property-based tests

Contributing

This is a complete, production-ready implementation. All phases (1-14) are complete.

For issues or questions, please refer to the original Go implementation at go.spyder.org/ds.

Acknowledgments

This Zig implementation is a faithful port of the Go reference implementation, maintaining:

  • All algorithms and data structures
  • Deterministic behavior and output
  • Comprehensive test coverage
  • Full API compatibility (adapted to Zig idioms)

Special thanks to the Zig community for the excellent language and tooling.

readme_content:
Zig Vulkan Compute Library

A production-grade GPU compute library for Zig, providing a clean, safe API for Vulkan compute operations. Version 0.6.0.

Status

Aspect Info

Platforms Linux, Windows (Vulkan-capable)

Features

Ray tracing (query only) :white_check_mark:
Mesh shaders (query only) :white_check_mark:

Requirements

  • Zig 0.15.1 or later
  • Vulkan runtime (optional at compile time, required at runtime for GPU operations)

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .vulkan = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/vulkan/-/archive/main/vulkan-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const vulkan_dep = b.dependency("vulkan", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("vulkan", vulkan_dep.module("vulkan"));

Quick Start

const std = @import("std");
const vulkan = @import("vulkan");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Check if Vulkan is available
    if (!vulkan.isAvailable()) {
        std.debug.print("Vulkan not available\n", .{});
        return error.VulkanUnavailable;
    }

    // Create a compute context
    var ctx = try vulkan.Context.init(allocator, .{
        .enable_validation = true,  // Enable for debugging
        .prefer_discrete = true,    // Prefer dedicated GPU
    });
    defer ctx.deinit();

    // Print device info
    const info = ctx.deviceInfo();
    std.debug.print("Using: {s}\n", .{info.getName()});

    // Create buffers
    var staging = try vulkan.Buffer.init(&ctx, 4096, .staging);
    defer staging.deinit(&ctx);

    var storage = try vulkan.Buffer.init(&ctx, 4096, .storage);
    defer storage.deinit(&ctx);

    // Write data to staging buffer
    var data = [_]f32{ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 };
    try staging.writeSlice(f32, &data);

    // Record and submit commands...
}

Probing the System

Check Vulkan availability without creating a full context:

var result = vulkan.probe(allocator);
defer result.deinit(allocator);

if (result.isAvailable()) {
    std.debug.print("Found {} device(s)\n", .{result.device_count});
    for (result.devices) |dev| {
        std.debug.print("  {s} - {s}\n", .{
            dev.getName(),
            @tagName(dev.device_type),
        });
    }
}

Documentation

  • Architecture Overview - Design and module structure

API Overview

Context

The main entry point for GPU compute operations.

var ctx = try vulkan.Context.init(allocator, .{
    .app_name = "my_app",
    .enable_validation = true,
    .prefer_discrete = true,
    .enable_timestamps = true,
});
defer ctx.deinit();

Buffers

GPU memory buffers with different usage patterns:

Usage Description Memory Type
.storage GPU read/write Device-local
.staging CPU to GPU upload Host-visible
.readback GPU to CPU download Host-visible
.uniform Constant data Host-visible

Pipelines

Load SPIR-V shaders and create compute pipelines:

var shader = try vulkan.ShaderModule.initFromBytes(&ctx, @embedFile("shader.spv"));
defer shader.deinit();

var layout = try vulkan.DescriptorSetLayout.init(&ctx, &.{
    .{ .binding = 0, .descriptor_type = .storage_buffer },
    .{ .binding = 1, .descriptor_type = .storage_buffer },
});
defer layout.deinit();

var pipeline = try vulkan.ComputePipeline.init(&ctx, shader, "main", layout, null);
defer pipeline.deinit();

Pipeline Cache

Disk-backed pipeline cache for faster startup:

var cache = try vulkan.PersistentPipelineCache.init(&ctx, .{
    .cache_path = "pipeline_cache.bin",
    .auto_save = true,
});
defer cache.deinit();  // Auto-saves on deinit

// Use cache for pipeline creation
var pipeline = try vulkan.ComputePipeline.initWithCache(&ctx, shader, "main", layout, null, cache.getHandle());

Command Recording

Record and submit GPU commands:

var cmd = try vulkan.CommandBuffer.init(&ctx);
defer cmd.deinit();

try cmd.begin();
pipeline.bind(cmd.getHandle());
pipeline.bindDescriptorSet(cmd.getHandle(), descriptor_set);
pipeline.dispatch(cmd.getHandle(), 64, 1, 1);
try cmd.end();

try vulkan.Submission.submitAndWait(&ctx, cmd);

Compute Graph

DAG-based task scheduling with automatic barriers:

var graph = vulkan.ComputeGraph.init(allocator, &ctx);
defer graph.deinit();

const input = try graph.registerResource("input", input_buffer, size);
const output = try graph.registerResource("output", output_buffer, size);

_ = try graph.addTask(.{
    .name = "process",
    .pipeline = pipeline,
    .workgroups = .{ 64, 1, 1 },
    .resources = &.{
        .{ .handle = input, .access = .read },
        .{ .handle = output, .access = .write },
    },
});

try graph.compile();
try graph.execute(cmd);

Memory Pressure Handling

Automatic resource eviction when memory is constrained:

var handler = try vulkan.MemoryPressureHandler.init(allocator, &ctx, .{
    .warning_threshold = 0.8,
    .critical_threshold = 0.95,
    .auto_evict = true,
});
defer handler.deinit();

handler.registerResource(.{
    .name = "cache_buffer",
    .priority = 0,  // Lower priority = evicted first
    .evict_fn = my_evict_callback,
});

Device Lost Recovery

Automatic recovery from GPU hangs:

var recovery = try vulkan.DeviceLostHandler.init(allocator, .{
    .max_recovery_attempts = 3,
    .recreate_pipelines = true,
});
defer recovery.deinit();

recovery.registerResource("my_buffer", buffer_ptr, recreate_buffer_fn, 10);

// On device lost, call:
try recovery.handleDeviceLost();  // Recreates resources by priority

Shader Compilation

Runtime GLSL/HLSL to SPIR-V:

// GLSL
if (vulkan.glsl.isCompilerAvailable()) {
    const result = try vulkan.glsl.compile(allocator, .{
        .source = glsl_source,
        .stage = .compute,
    });
    defer result.deinit();
    // Use result.spirv
}

// HLSL (via DXC)
if (vulkan.glsl.isHlslCompilerAvailable()) {
    const result = try vulkan.glsl.compileHlsl(allocator, .{
        .source = hlsl_source,
        .stage = .compute,
        .shader_model = .sm_6_5,
    });
    defer result.deinit();
}

Error Handling

All errors are returned as Zig errors with descriptive names:

const ctx = vulkan.Context.init(allocator, .{}) catch |err| {
    std.debug.print("Error: {s}\n", .{vulkan.describeError(err)});

    // Get recovery suggestions
    const suggestions = vulkan.Diagnostics.getSuggestions(err);
    for (suggestions) |s| {
        std.debug.print("  Suggestion: {s}\n", .{s});
    }
    return err;
};

Common errors:

  • VulkanUnavailable - Vulkan loader not found
  • NoDevices - No Vulkan devices found
  • NoComputeQueue - No compute-capable queue
  • OutOfDeviceMemory - GPU memory exhausted
  • DeviceLost - GPU crashed or hung

Extension Capabilities

Query device capabilities:

const caps = vulkan.queryAllCapabilities(&ctx);

if (caps.subgroup.supported) {
    std.debug.print("Subgroup size: {}\n", .{caps.subgroup.subgroup_size});
}

if (caps.cooperative_matrix.supported) {
    // Use cooperative matrices for ML workloads
}

// Memory budget
const budget = vulkan.queryMemoryBudget(&ctx);
for (0..budget.heap_count) |i| {
    std.debug.print("Heap {}: {} MB / {} MB\n", .{
        i,
        budget.heaps[i].usage / (1024 * 1024),
        budget.heaps[i].budget / (1024 * 1024),
    });
}

Observability

vulkan ships an opt-in OpenTelemetry seam. Build with -Dwith_otel=true to compile in instrumentation; the default (-Dwith_otel=false) leaves every span site as a comptime no-op so the optimizer eliminates the entry/exit calls and the otel dependency is never fetched.

Public Vulkan boundaries emit exactly one span per call, named vulkan.{operation} with the OpenTelemetry gpu.* semantic-convention attributes:

  • gpu.system = "vulkan"
  • gpu.operation = <method> (e.g. queue_submit, device_wait_idle, pipeline_create, queue_wait_idle)

The instrumented entry points are:

Operation Span name Extra attributes
Submission.submit vulkan.queue_submit vulkan.cmd_buffer_count
QueueManager.submitCompute vulkan.queue_submit vulkan.queue_family="compute", vulkan.cmd_buffer_count
QueueManager.submitTransfer vulkan.queue_submit vulkan.queue_family="transfer" (or compute fallback), vulkan.cmd_buffer_count
QueueManager.submitAsyncCompute vulkan.queue_submit vulkan.queue_family="async_compute" (or compute fallback), vulkan.cmd_buffer_count
Submission.waitQueueIdle vulkan.queue_wait_idle --
Context.waitIdle vulkan.device_wait_idle --
ComputePipeline.init vulkan.pipeline_create -- (no shader bytecode or pipeline state in attrs)

Per-record command-buffer ops are deliberately NOT instrumented (high volume, low signal). Telemetry is non-fatal: every emit and attribute write is catch {}-discarded so a failed exporter or attribute-set OOM can never propagate into GPU operations.

zig build test                  # default: -Dwith_otel=false (no-op)
zig build test -Dwith_otel=true # otel compiled in, spans emitted

When enabled, the consumer's process bootstrap calls vulkan.observability_init.Otel.init(allocator, "service-name") and parks the returned value at a stable address (a var in main or a heap allocation), then calls installGlobals(&that_value) so the seam can publish its tracer pointer.

For the full integration recipe and template files, see otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md in the otel repo.

  4. Ensure formatting: zig fmt --check src tests bench examples
  5. Submit a merge request

name: cuda
description: A comprehensive CUDA compute library for Zig providing GPU memory management, kernel compilation/launching, device probing, and profiling capabilities
readme_content:
cuda - Zig CUDA Compute Library

A comprehensive CUDA compute library for Zig with graceful degradation, dynamic driver loading, and support for NVIDIA Blackwell architectures.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.0+
Platforms Linux (x86_64, aarch64)

Features

Core Capabilities

  • Dynamic Driver Loading: Runtime loading of CUDA driver via dlopen/LoadLibrary (no compile-time NVIDIA SDK required)
  • Graceful Degradation: Never panics when CUDA unavailable - returns errors for graceful handling
  • NVIDIA Blackwell Support: Full support for SM 10.0 (GB100/GB102/GB202) architectures
  • Linux-Native: Supported on Linux (x86_64, aarch64) with dynamic driver detection. Windows is not yet supported and macOS is unsupported (NVIDIA discontinued macOS CUDA).
  • Zero Dependencies: Pure Zig implementation using only the standard library
  • Memory Pooling: Efficient buffer reuse to minimize allocation overhead
  • PTX Loading: Load and execute PTX (Parallel Thread Execution) kernels
  • NVRTC Integration: Optional JIT compilation of CUDA C to PTX at runtime
  • Performance Profiling: Built-in CUDA event-based timing and bandwidth measurement

GPU Support

  • Device Enumeration: Automatic detection and enumeration of all CUDA devices
  • Compute Capabilities: SM 3.0 (Kepler) through SM 10.0 (Blackwell)
  • Architecture Detection: Automatic architecture name and feature detection
  • Multi-GPU Ready: Support for device selection and multi-context workflows

Memory Management

  • Device Memory: Standard GPU memory allocation
  • Pinned Memory: Page-locked host memory for faster transfers
  • Unified Memory: Managed memory accessible from CPU and GPU
  • Async Transfers: Overlapped H2D/D2H transfers with streams
  • Memory Statistics: Track allocations, transfers, and pool usage

In the high-level context API, createBuffer honors MemoryKind:

const device_buf = try ctx.createBuffer(1024, .device);
defer ctx.destroyBuffer(device_buf);

const unified_buf = try ctx.createBuffer(1024, .unified);
defer ctx.destroyBuffer(unified_buf);

const pinned = try ctx.createPinnedBuffer(1024);
defer ctx.destroyPinnedBuffer(pinned);

Streams and Events

  • CUDA Streams: Async kernel execution and memory operations
  • CUDA Events: Synchronization and timing measurement
  • Stream Pools: Reusable stream management
  • Event Timers: High-precision GPU timing

Requirements

  • Zig 0.16.0 or later
  • NVIDIA GPU with CUDA drivers (optional - library works without GPU)
  • CUDA Driver 11.0+ recommended for full feature support

Installation

Add cuda as a dependency in your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .cuda = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/cuda/-/archive/main/cuda-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const cuda_dep = b.dependency("cuda", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});

exe.root_module.addImport("cuda", cuda_dep.module("cuda"));

Quick Start

Check CUDA Availability

const std = @import("std");
const cuda = @import("cuda");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Quick availability check
    if (!cuda.isAvailable()) {
        std.debug.print("CUDA is not available\n", .{});
        return;
    }

    // Detailed probe with diagnostics
    var result = try cuda.probe(allocator);
    defer result.deinit(allocator);

    if (result.available) {
        std.debug.print("Found {} CUDA device(s)\n", .{result.device_count});
        for (result.devices) |dev| {
            std.debug.print("  {}: {s} ({s})\n", .{
                dev.id,
                dev.getName(),
                dev.getArchName(),
            });
        }
    } else {
        std.debug.print("CUDA unavailable: {s}\n", .{result.getErrorMessage()});
    }
}

Basic GPU Compute

const std = @import("std");
const cuda = @import("cuda");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Create CUDA context
    var ctx = cuda.Context.init(allocator, .{}) catch |err| {
        std.debug.print("Failed to create context: {}\n", .{err});
        return;
    };
    defer ctx.deinit();

    // Allocate device memory
    const buffer = try ctx.createBuffer(1024 * @sizeOf(f32), .device);
    defer ctx.destroyBuffer(buffer);

    // Upload data
    var host_data: [1024]f32 = undefined;
    for (&host_data, 0..) |*v, i| {
        v.* = @floatFromInt(i);
    }
    try ctx.memcpyH2D(buffer, std.mem.sliceAsBytes(&host_data));

    // Download results
    var result: [1024]f32 = undefined;
    try ctx.memcpyD2H(std.mem.sliceAsBytes(&result), buffer);
}

Running a PTX Kernel

const cuda = @import("cuda");

// PTX kernel source
const kernel_ptx =
    \\.version 7.0
    \\.target sm_52
    \\.address_size 64
    \\
    \\.visible .entry my_kernel(
    \\    .param .u64 data,
    \\    .param .u32 n
    \\)
    \\{
    \\    // kernel code...
    \\    ret;
    \\}
;

pub fn main() !void {
    // ... context setup ...

    // Load PTX module
    const module = try ctx.createModulePtx(kernel_ptx);
    defer ctx.destroyModule(module);

    // Get kernel function
    const kernel = try ctx.getKernel(module, "my_kernel");

    // Set up arguments
    var data_ptr: u64 = buffer.ptr;
    var n: u32 = 1024;

    var args = cuda.KernelArgs(4){};
    args.addPtr(&data_ptr);
    args.addPtr(&n);

    // Launch kernel
    try ctx.launch(kernel, .{
        .grid = .{ 4, 1, 1 },
        .block = .{ 256, 1, 1 },
    }, args.getArgs());

    // Synchronize
    try ctx.syncAll();
}

Building

# Build the library
zig build

# Run all tests (GPU tests skip gracefully if unavailable)
zig build test --summary all

# Run specific test suites
zig build test-types      # Type definitions
zig build test-driver     # Driver loading
zig build test-probe      # Device probing
zig build test-memory     # Memory management
zig build test-stream     # Streams and events
zig build test-module     # PTX loading
zig build test-context    # Context API
zig build test-integration # Full integration tests

# Build with optimization
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast

# Build examples
zig build examples

# Run benchmarks
zig build benchmarks -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
./zig-out/bin/cuda_benchmark

Using the Makefile

# Build and test
make

# Quick probe for CUDA
make probe

# Run benchmarks
make bench

# Development workflow
make dev

# See all targets
make help

Project Structure

src/
├── cuda.zig             # Public API entry point
└── cuda/
    ├── types.zig        # CUDA types, errors, ComputeArch
    ├── driver.zig       # Dynamic CUDA driver loading
    ├── probe.zig        # Device detection and diagnostics
    ├── memory.zig       # Buffer management with pooling
    ├── stream.zig       # Streams, events, timers
    ├── module.zig       # PTX/CUBIN loading, kernels
    ├── context.zig      # High-level Context API
    └── profiler.zig     # Performance profiling
tests/
├── integration.zig      # GPU integration tests
benchmarks/
├── main.zig             # Benchmark suite (H2D, D2H, launch overhead)
examples/
├── device_info.zig      # Device enumeration example
└── vector_add.zig       # Complete CUDA workflow example

Architecture Support

Architecture Compute Capability Status
Kepler SM 3.0 - 3.7 Supported
Maxwell SM 5.0 - 5.3 Supported
Pascal SM 6.0 - 6.2 Supported
Volta SM 7.0 Supported
Turing SM 7.5 Supported
Ampere SM 8.0 - 8.9 Supported
Ada Lovelace SM 8.9 Supported
Hopper SM 9.0 Supported
Blackwell SM 10.0 Supported

Cross-Compilation

Linux (x86_64, aarch64) is the supported target:

# Linux x64
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu

# Linux ARM64 (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson)
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu

Non-Linux targets are not supported:

  • Windows is not yet supported - the runtime currently relies on Linux-specific assumptions and does not compile cleanly for Windows.
  • macOS is unsupported - NVIDIA discontinued CUDA for macOS. The runtime probe reports platform_not_supported on any non-Linux platform.

Graceful Degradation

The library is designed to work on systems without CUDA:

// This never panics - returns false if CUDA unavailable
if (!cuda.isAvailable()) {
    // Fall back to CPU implementation
    return cpuCompute();
}

// Detailed diagnostics available
var probe = try cuda.probe(allocator);
if (!probe.available) {
    switch (probe.unavailable_reason) {
        .driver_not_found => // CUDA driver not installed
        .no_devices => // No NVIDIA GPUs found
        .kernel_module_not_loaded => // nvidia.ko not loaded
        .platform_not_supported => // Platform not supported (non-Linux)
        // ... handle each case
    }
}

Performance Considerations

  • Memory Pooling: Buffers are pooled and reused to minimize cuMemAlloc overhead
  • Pinned Memory: Use .host_pinned for faster H2D/D2H transfers
  • Streams: Use streams for overlapped transfers and kernel execution
  • Batch Transfers: Minimize the number of small transfers

Observability

This library exposes an OpenTelemetry seam for tracing host-device boundary calls (kernel launches, memcpy H2D/D2H/D2D, synchronizes, and device allocations). The seam is gated behind a build flag so disabled builds pay zero overhead and contain zero otel symbols.

Enabling

# Default: otel disabled. The dependency is never fetched and the
# produced artifacts contain zero otel/observability symbols.
zig build

# Enable: otel compiled in, spans emitted to the OTLP HTTP endpoint
# at http://localhost:4318 (overridable via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*).
zig build -Dwith_otel=true

When -Dwith_otel=true is in effect, every Context.memcpyH2D, Context.memcpyD2H, Context.memcpyD2D, Context.memcpyH2DAsync, Context.memcpyD2HAsync, Context.launch, Context.launch1D, Context.launchSync, Context.sync, Context.createBuffer, and Context.destroyBuffer call emits a span named cuda.{operation} with the following attributes:

Attribute Value Notes
gpu.system "cuda" Always present
gpu.operation e.g. "memcpy_h2d", "launch_kernel" Always present
cuda.bytes byte count Memcpy + alloc only; omitted for sync/launch

Span kind is client (the host is the "client" of the GPU device). GPU-side execution time is intentionally not spanned — spans cover the host-side enqueue/wait only. Async memcpy spans cover the enqueue call, not the device-side completion. Kernel argument values are deliberately excluded from span attributes (secrets / PII risk).

Bootstrapping

Park an Otel value at a stable address and publish its globals once at process start:

const cuda = @import("cuda");

pub fn main() !void {
    var otel_inst = try cuda.observability_init.Otel.init(allocator, "my-cuda-app");
    defer otel_inst.deinit();
    otel_inst.installGlobals();

    // ... cuda work; spans flow through the seam automatically.
}

OTEL_* env vars (sampler, exporter endpoint, service name, …) work as the otel SDK specifies. Default sampler is parentbased_traceidratio @ 5%; default exporter is otlp over http/protobuf to http://localhost:4318.

Verifying the no-op invariant

The otel repo ships a script that builds the consumer with -Dwith_otel=false and greps the resulting artifacts for any otel/observability symbols. From the otel repo root:

otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh cuda

See otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md for the full integration recipe and invariants.

name: strings
description: ZigStr - A comprehensive Unicode string library for Zig with SSO, full Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD), text segmentation, collation, regex, fuzzy matching, and support for legacy encodings (CJK, Windows code pages, ISO-8859)
readme_content:
ZigStr - Unicode String Library for Zig

A comprehensive Unicode string manipulation library for Zig with full UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32 support, Small String Optimization (SSO), and Unicode 15.1 compliance.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.15.1+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows (cross-compilation verified in CI)

Features

  • UTF-8 Internal Storage - Efficient storage like Go and Rust
  • Small String Optimization (SSO) - Strings ≤23 bytes stored inline without heap allocation
  • Full Unicode Support
    • UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 encoding/decoding
    • Unicode normalization (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD)
    • Grapheme cluster segmentation (UAX #29)
    • Word and sentence boundaries (UAX #29)
    • Case mapping and folding
    • Unicode Collation Algorithm (UTS #10)
    • Script detection (UAX #24)
    • Basic BiDi direction detection (partial UAX #9)
    • Line breaking (UAX #14)
    • Identifier syntax (UAX #31)
  • Go-style String Functions - Familiar API for Go developers
  • SIMD Acceleration - AVX2/AVX-512 hardware acceleration
  • String Interning - Memory-efficient string deduplication
  • Advanced Data Structures
    • Rope for large string manipulation
    • Memory-mapped strings
    • Lazy normalization
  • Extended Features
    • Regular expressions
    • Fuzzy matching (Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, etc.)
    • Phonetic algorithms (Soundex, Metaphone, Double Metaphone, NYSIIS)
    • Locale-specific formatting (20+ locales)
    • ICU compatibility layer
  • Legacy Encoding Support
    • Windows code pages (CP1250-1258, CP437, CP850)
    • ISO-8859 family (1-16)
    • Chinese: GB2312, GBK, GB18030
    • Japanese: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP
    • Korean: EUC-KR, CP949
    • Traditional Chinese: Big5, Big5-HKSCS

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .strings = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/strings/-/archive/main/strings-main.tar.gz",
        // Add the hash after first build attempt
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const strings = b.dependency("strings", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("strings", strings.module("strings"));

Quick Start

const std = @import("std");
const strings = @import("strings");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Create a string (uses SSO for small strings)
    var str = try strings.String.fromSlice(allocator, "Hello, World!");
    defer str.deinit();

    // String operations
    std.debug.print("Length: {}\n", .{str.len()});
    std.debug.print("Is inline (SSO): {}\n", .{str.isInline()});

    // Search
    if (str.contains("World")) {
        std.debug.print("Found 'World'!\n", .{});
    }

    // Case conversion
    var upper = try str.toUpper();
    defer upper.deinit();
    std.debug.print("Upper: {s}\n", .{upper.bytes()});

    // UTF-16 conversion
    const utf16 = try str.toUtf16(.little);
    defer allocator.free(utf16);
}

Core Types

String

UTF-8 backed string with SSO:

var str = try strings.String.fromSlice(allocator, "Hello");
defer str.deinit();

// SSO: strings ≤23 bytes are stored inline
try std.testing.expect(str.isInline());

StringBuilder

Efficient string concatenation:

var builder = strings.StringBuilder.init(allocator);
defer builder.deinit();

try builder.append("Hello");
try builder.appendByte(' ');
try builder.append("World");

const result = builder.slice(); // "Hello World"

StringPool

String interning for memory efficiency:

var pool = strings.StringPool.init(allocator);
defer pool.deinit();

const s1 = try pool.intern("hello");
const s2 = try pool.intern("hello");
// s1.ptr == s2.ptr (same memory)

Unicode Operations

Grapheme Clusters

// Count user-perceived characters
const text = "e\xCC\x81"; // e + combining acute = é
const count = strings.grapheme.count(text);
// count == 1 (one grapheme cluster)

Case Conversion

const upper = try strings.toUpper(allocator, "hello");
defer allocator.free(upper);
// upper == "HELLO"

const lower = try strings.toLower(allocator, "WORLD");
defer allocator.free(lower);
// lower == "world"

Collation

// Case-insensitive comparison
const eq = strings.collation.equals("Hello", "HELLO", .{ .strength = .primary });
// eq == true

Encoding Detection

const result = strings.detection.detect("\xEF\xBB\xBFHello");
// result.encoding == .utf8
// result.has_bom == true

Go-style Functions

For developers familiar with Go's strings package:

// Cut - split at first separator
const result = strings.cut("hello,world", ",");
// result.before == "hello", result.after == "world"

// Fields - split on whitespace
var fields = strings.fields(allocator, "  hello   world  ");
defer fields.deinit();
// fields.items == ["hello", "world"]

// TrimPrefix/TrimSuffix
const trimmed = strings.trimPrefix("hello.txt", "hello");
// trimmed == ".txt"

Building

# Build library
zig build

# Run all tests
zig build test

# Run specific test suite
zig build test-string
zig build test-unicode
zig build test-acceptance

Thread Safety

  • All pure functions (encoding, decoding, searching, comparison) are thread-safe when operating on separate data.
  • String, String16, StringBuilder, and StringPool are not internally synchronized -- callers must provide external synchronization for concurrent access to the same instance.
  • The parallel module (parallelCount, parallelMap, parallelEditDistanceBatch, parallelFuzzySearch) is safe to call concurrently from multiple threads. Each call must use distinct output/results slices; read-only input slices may be shared. The global thread pool is lazily initialized with mutex protection.
  • See Architecture - Thread Safety for full details.

Documentation

  • API Reference
  • Usage Examples
  • Architecture
  • Roadmap

Project Status

v0.1.0 - Feature Complete

All planned features have been implemented:

  • UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, ASCII, Latin-1 encoding/decoding
  • Small String Optimization (SSO)
  • Unicode Character Database tables (simplified for some categories)
  • Text segmentation (grapheme, word, sentence)
  • Unicode normalization (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD)
  • Case conversion and folding
  • Collation (ASCII/Latin-1)
  • Script detection, basic BiDi direction detection, line breaking, identifier syntax
  • SIMD acceleration (AVX2/AVX-512)
  • String interning, rope data structure, memory-mapped strings
  • Regular expressions, fuzzy matching, phonetic algorithms
  • Locale-specific formatting, ICU compatibility layer
  • Legacy encodings (Windows CP, ISO-8859, CJK)

See ROADMAP.md for full details.

Contributing

Contributions welcome! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

Priority areas:

  1. Testing - Add Unicode conformance test vectors
  2. Documentation - Examples and tutorials
  3. Bug fixes - Report and fix any issues
  4. Performance - Profile and optimize critical paths
  5. Additional locales - Expand locale support

License

Apache-2.0 License - See LICENSE for details.

References

  • Unicode Standard
  • UAX #15: Normalization Forms
  • UAX #29: Text Segmentation
  • UTS #10: Collation Algorithm
  • Zig Language

name: uri
description: RFC 3986 compliant URI/URL parsing and manipulation library for Zig. Zero-copy parsing, URI resolution, normalization, percent-encoding, URN support (RFC 8141), and resource registry.
readme_content:
URI

RFC 3986 compliant URI/URL parsing and manipulation library for Zig.

Project Status: Active Development Current Version: v0.1.5 GitLab: devnw/zig/uri

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.0+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • RFC Compliant: Strict adherence to RFC 3986 (URI Generic Syntax) and RFC 8141 (URN)
  • Minimal Dependencies: Core parsing uses only Zig standard library; optional thread-pool dependency for parallel batch operations
  • Zero-Copy Parsing: No allocations for basic parsing operations
  • Cross-Platform: Works on all Zig-supported targets
  • Full Component Access: Scheme, authority, userinfo, host, port, path, query, fragment
  • URI Resolution: RFC 3986 Section 5 reference resolution algorithm
  • Normalization: Case, percent-encoding, path, and scheme-based normalization per RFC 3986 Section 6
  • Percent-Encoding: Complete encode/decode support
  • Parse Options: Strict/allow_spaces/iri_mode validation applied on input
  • Component-Aware Encoding: Percent-encoding respects URI component rules
  • URN Support: Full RFC 8141 URN parsing with NID, NSS, and r/q/f-components
  • Resource Registry: Document storage with fetch callbacks and anchor support

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .uri = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/uri/-/archive/main/uri-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const uri_dep = b.dependency("uri", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("uri", uri_dep.module("uri"));

Quick Start

Parse a URI

const uri = @import("uri");

pub fn main() !void {
    const parsed = try uri.parse("https://user:pass@example.com:8080/path?query=value#fragment");

    // Access components
    std.debug.print("Scheme: {s}\n", .{parsed.scheme.?});        // "https"
    std.debug.print("Host: {s}\n", .{parsed.host.?});            // "example.com"
    std.debug.print("Port: {d}\n", .{parsed.port.?});            // 8080
    std.debug.print("Path: {s}\n", .{parsed.path});              // "/path"
    std.debug.print("Query: {s}\n", .{parsed.query.?});          // "query=value"
    std.debug.print("Fragment: {s}\n", .{parsed.fragment.?});    // "fragment"
}

Parse a URN

const parsed = try uri.parse("urn:isbn:0451450523");

std.debug.print("NID: {s}\n", .{parsed.urn.?.nid.?});   // "isbn"
std.debug.print("NSS: {s}\n", .{parsed.urn.?.nss.?});   // "0451450523"

Resolve URI References

const allocator = std.heap.page_allocator;
const base = try uri.parse("http://example.com/a/b/c");
const reference = try uri.parse("../d");
const resolved = try uri.resolve(allocator, base, reference);
// Result: "http://example.com/a/d"

Percent-Encoding

// Encode
const encoded = try uri.percentEncode(allocator, "hello world!", .path);
// Result: "hello%20world%21"

// Decode
const decoded = try uri.percentDecode(allocator, "hello%20world%21");
// Result: "hello world!"

Resource Registry

var reg = uri.Registry.init(allocator);
defer reg.deinit();

try reg.register("https://example.com/schema.json", "{\"type\":\"object\"}", "application/json");
const resource = try reg.get("https://example.com/schema.json", false);

URI Components

         foo://user:pass@example.com:8042/over/there?name=ferret#nose
         \_/   \________________________/\_________/ \_________/ \__/
          |              |                    |            |       |
       scheme        authority              path        query   fragment
          |   _________________|________________
         / \ /                                  \
         urn:example:animal:ferret:nose

The authority component breaks down into:

         userinfo       host          port
         +--+---+ +------+------+ +---+---+
         user:pass@www.example.com:8080

Documentation

  • API Reference - Complete API documentation
  • RFC Compliance - Detailed RFC compliance status

Roadmap

v0.1.0 - Foundation ✅

Core URI parsing and manipulation functionality.


RFC 3986 URI parsing (#1)
URI reference resolution (#2)
Basic normalization (#3)
Percent encoding/decoding (#4)
URN support - RFC 8141 (#5)
Resource registry (#6)
Debug utilities (#7)

v0.2.0 - Enhanced Parsing

Improved validation and encoding options.


ParseOptions implementation (#8)
Component-specific encoding rules (#9)
Enhanced percent-encoding normalization (#10)
Query string parsing (#11)
URI builder API (#12)

v0.3.0 - IRI Support

RFC 3987 Internationalized Resource Identifiers.


Unicode support in path/query (#13)
IRI ↔ URI conversion (#14)
Unicode normalization (#15)

v0.4.0 - IPv6 Enhancements

RFC 6874 IPv6 Zone ID support.


Zone ID parsing (#16)
IPv6 address validation (#17)
IPvFuture support (#18)

v1.0.0 - Stable Release

Production-ready release.


WHATWG URL Standard compatibility (#19)
Complete documentation (#20)
Performance benchmarks (#21)
CI/CD pipeline (#22)
Package publishing setup (#26)
Scheme-based normalization (#29)
Streaming parser (#27)
WebAssembly target (#28)

RFC Compliance

RFC Title Status Details
RFC 3986 URI Generic Syntax Implemented #1, #2, #3
RFC 8141 URN Syntax Implemented #5
RFC 3987 IRI Syntax Planned #13, #14, #15
RFC 6874 IPv6 Zone ID Planned #16, #17, #18
WHATWG URL Standard Partial #19

See RFC_COMPLIANCE.md for detailed compliance information.

Building

# Build
zig build

# Run tests
zig build test

# Run RFC test vectors
zig build test-vectors

# Run acceptance tests

# Run dataset tests (500+ URIs)

# Run all tests
zig build test-all

Or use Make:

make          # Build and test
make test     # Run tests
make dev      # Development workflow (fmt + check + test)
make help     # Show all targets

Development

With Nix

make dev

Requirements

  • Zig 0.16.0 or compatible

Cross-Platform Support

The library supports all Zig target platforms:

  • Linux (x86_64, ARM64, ARM, RISC-V)
  • macOS (x86_64, ARM64)
  • Windows (x86_64, ARM64)
  • FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD
  • And more...

Contributing

Getting Started

name: repl
description: A cross-platform, feature-rich REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) library for Zig with Emacs/Vi keybindings, command history, tab completion, multi-line input, and colored output
readme_content:
Zig REPL Library

A cross-platform, feature-rich REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) library for Zig.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.x
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • Raw terminal mode with cleanup on normal exit, on SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and on suspend/resume (SIGTSTP/SIGCONT)
  • Emacs and Vi keybindings - switch modes at runtime
  • Persistent command history - saved to disk, searchable
  • Tab completion - extensible completion system
  • Multi-line input - automatic detection of incomplete statements
  • Undo support -- bounded undo stack with Ctrl+_ (Emacs) and u (Vi normal mode)
  • Bracketed paste mode - properly handles pasted text
  • Colored output - 16-color support with semantic helpers
  • Cross-platform - Linux, macOS, and Windows support

Installation

Add the library to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .repl = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/repl/-/archive/main/repl-main.tar.gz",
        // Add the hash after first build attempt
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const repl_dep = b.dependency("repl", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("repl", repl_dep.module("repl"));

Quick Start

const std = @import("std");
const repl = @import("repl");

pub fn main() !void {
    var da: std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{}) = .init;
    defer _ = da.deinit();

    try repl.Repl.run(.{
        .allocator = da.allocator(),
        .prompt = ">>> ",
        .run_fn = runCommand,
    });
}

fn runCommand(
    _: ?*anyopaque,
    _: std.mem.Allocator,
    input: []const u8,
    _: *repl.HistoryStore,
) anyerror!bool {
    if (std.mem.eql(u8, input, "quit")) {
        return false; // exit REPL
    }

    const out = repl.terminalWriter();
    try out.print("You entered: {s}\n", .{input});
    return true; // continue REPL
}

Configuration Options

The Repl.run() function accepts a configuration struct with these options:

Option Type Default Description
allocator Allocator required Memory allocator
prompt []const u8 "> " Primary prompt string
continuation_prompt []const u8 "... " Multi-line continuation prompt
keymap Keymap .emacs .emacs or .vi
history_enabled bool true Enable command history
app_name []const u8 "repl" Application name (used for default history file path)
history_path ?[]const u8 null Custom history file path (overrides default)
max_history usize 5000 Maximum history entries kept in memory and persisted
run_fn ?RunFn null Command handler callback (see Quick Start)
is_complete_fn ?IsCompleteFn null Multi-line input detection
complete_fn ?CompleteFn null Tab completion callback
welcome_fn ?WelcomeFn null Welcome message printer (called before entering raw mode)
verbose bool false Show verbose output
user_context ?*anyopaque null User context passed to run_fn callback

Note: Repl.Options is for REPL initialization. The separate Config type (repl.Config) provides application-level persistence via loadFromFile() and saveToFile(). These are separate by design -- Config is not auto-loaded by Repl.run(). Applications that want config file support should load a Config, then map its fields to Options when calling Repl.run().

Terminal Output

The library provides TerminalWriter for proper terminal output in raw mode. Use the convenience function repl.terminalWriter() or construct one from a file handle:

const repl = @import("repl");

// Create a TerminalWriter for stdout
const out = repl.terminalWriter();

// Basic output (handles \n -> \r\n conversion automatically)
try out.write("Hello, world!\n");
try out.writeLine("This adds a newline");
try out.print("Formatted: {d}\n", .{42});

// Colored output
try out.writeColored(.green, "Success!");
try out.writeColored(.red, "Error!");

// Styled output (style, color, text)
try out.writeBold("Important");
try out.writeStyled(.italic, .default, "Emphasized");

// Semantic helpers
try out.writeError("Something went wrong");    // Red "Error: " prefix
try out.writeWarning("Be careful");            // Yellow "Warning: " prefix
try out.writeSuccess("Operation completed");   // Green message
try out.writeInfo("FYI");                      // Cyan message

// Screen control
try out.clearScreen();
try out.clearLine();

// Manual color control
try out.setColor(.blue);
try out.write("Blue text");
try out.resetStyle();

Available Colors

const Color = enum {
    default,
    black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white,
    bright_black, bright_red, bright_green, bright_yellow,
    bright_blue, bright_magenta, bright_cyan, bright_white,
};

Available Styles

const Style = enum {
    reset, bold, dim, italic, underline,
};

Tab Completion

Implement tab completion by providing a complete_fn:

const commands = [_][]const u8{ "help", "quit", "history", "clear", "echo" };

fn completeCommand(
    prefix: []const u8,
    ctx: *repl.CompletionContext,
) void {
    for (commands) |cmd| {
        if (std.mem.startsWith(u8, cmd, prefix)) {
            ctx.addCandidate(cmd) catch {};
        }
    }
}

// In configuration:
.complete_fn = completeCommand,

Multi-line Input

Enable multi-line input by providing an is_complete_fn:

fn isComplete(input: []const u8) bool {
    const trimmed = std.mem.trim(u8, input, " \t\n\r");

    // Continue if line ends with backslash
    if (std.mem.endsWith(u8, trimmed, "\\")) return false;

    // Use built-in bracket balancing
    return repl.isBalanced(input);
}

// In configuration:
.is_complete_fn = isComplete,

The library provides these parsing utilities:

  • repl.isBalanced(input) - Check if brackets/braces/parens are balanced
  • repl.needsContinuation(input) - Check for trailing operators
  • repl.isComplete(input) - Combined check for complete statements

Command History

The HistoryStore is passed to your run_fn callback:

fn runCommand(
    _: ?*anyopaque,
    _: std.mem.Allocator,
    input: []const u8,
    hist: *repl.HistoryStore,
) anyerror!bool {
    // Show history count
    const count = hist.count();
    _ = count;

    // Search history
    if (hist.searchBackward("pattern", null)) |result| {
        _ = result;
    }

    // Clear history
    hist.clear();

    return true;
}

History is automatically saved if history_path is configured or if history_enabled is true (which uses a default path based on app_name).

Keybindings

Emacs Mode (default)

Key Action
Ctrl+A Move to beginning of line
Ctrl+E Move to end of line
Ctrl+B Move cursor left
Ctrl+F Move cursor right
Ctrl+D Delete character / EOF on empty line
Ctrl+K Kill to end of line
Ctrl+U Kill to beginning of line
Ctrl+W Kill previous word
Ctrl+Y Yank (paste) killed text
Ctrl+P Previous history
Ctrl+N Next history
Ctrl+R Reverse history search
Ctrl+L Clear screen
Ctrl+_ Undo last edit
Tab Trigger completion

Vi Mode

Key Action
Esc Enter normal mode
i Enter insert mode
a Enter insert mode after cursor
h/l Move left/right
0/$ Move to beginning/end of line
w/b Move word forward/backward
x Delete character
dd Delete line
u Undo last edit (normal mode)
j/k Next/previous history
/ Search history

Running the Example

# Build and run with Emacs bindings (default)
zig build run

# Run with Vi bindings
zig build run -- --vi

# Build and run tests
zig build test

API Reference

Core Types

  • Repl - Main REPL runner (call Repl.run(options) to start)
  • ReplState - Internal state (exposed for advanced use)
  • Config - Application configuration (persistent via loadFromFile/saveToFile)
  • KeyEvent - Parsed key events
  • KeyAction - Internal action enum for key dispatch (not returned by user callbacks)
  • Keymap - Keymap selection (.emacs or .vi)
  • CompleteFn - Tab completion callback function type
  • SyntheticKey - Named constants for special keys (Insert, Delete, Page Up, Page Down)
  • Format - Output format enum (.text, .json, .csv, .table)

Platform Utilities

  • TerminalWriter - Terminal output with raw mode handling
  • terminalWriter() - Create a TerminalWriter for a given file handle
  • Color - Terminal colors
  • Style - Text styles (bold, dim, italic, underline)
  • getStdinHandle() - Get a handle to stdin for direct I/O operations
  • getStdoutHandle() - Get a handle to stdout for direct I/O operations
  • getStderrHandle() - Get a handle to stderr for direct I/O operations
  • isStdinTty() - Check if stdin is a TTY
  • isStdoutTty() - Check if stdout is a TTY
  • isStderrTty() - Check if stderr is a TTY

History

  • HistoryStore - Command history storage and search

Completion

  • CompletionContext - Completion results builder

Parsing

  • isComplete(input) - Check if input is a complete statement
  • isBalanced(input) - Check bracket balance
  • needsContinuation(input) - Check for continuation operators

Version

  • version - Library version string (e.g., "0.1.0")
  • version_major - Major version number
  • version_minor - Minor version number
  • version_patch - Patch version number

Building

# Debug build
zig build

# Release build
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe

# Run tests
zig build test

# Check formatting
zig fmt --check src/ tests/ examples/ build.zig

Observability

This library ships an optional OpenTelemetry seam, gated behind -Dwith_otel=<bool> (default false).

When -Dwith_otel=false (the default) the seam collapses to a comptime-known no-op: every public helper in repl.observability returns a zero-sized Span{}, the otel dependency is never resolved, and the produced artifact contains zero otel symbols (verified by otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh).

When -Dwith_otel=true, every accepted REPL line emits one internal-kind span per eval cycle. Each span is named "repl.eval" and reports outcome via setStatus(.ok | .@"error", ""). On failure, a bounded-cardinality repl.eval.error_kind attribute is attached carrying the handler's error name (e.g. "OutOfMemory", "InvalidInput") -- never the error message body.

PII INVARIANT: the raw user-typed input is never attached as a span attribute. REPL inputs may contain passwords, tokens, file paths, or other sensitive data, so the seam refuses to accept user-supplied strings on its public surface. Operators who want richer telemetry on specific commands (where the command vocabulary is fixed and bounded) can attach their own attributes via the underlying otel.api.trace.Span.setStringAttribute after the seam returns.

Bootstrap from your application entry point:

const std = @import("std");
const repl = @import("repl");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa: std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}) = .{};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();

    var otel = try repl.observability_init.Otel.init(gpa.allocator(), "my-repl");
    otel.installGlobals();
    defer otel.deinit();

    try repl.Repl.run(.{
        .allocator = gpa.allocator(),
        .prompt = ">>> ",
        .run_fn = runCommand, // each accepted line emits one "repl.eval" span
    });
}

Configuration follows the OpenTelemetry environment-variable contract (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, etc). Defaults: parentbased_traceidratio @ 5%, OTLP/HTTP to http://localhost:4318.

Verification gates (all three must pass):

zig build test                                              # default flag = false
zig build test -Dwith_otel=true                             # flag on
otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh --worktree <name> repl # symbol-leak check

See otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md for the full recipe.

Roadmap

Development is tracked through GitLab issues organized into milestones:

Current Priorities

Priority Issue Description
High #2 Add comprehensive unit tests
High #12 Add Unicode and wide character support
High #20 Write API documentation
Medium #10 Add syntax highlighting support
Medium #3 Add integration tests

Milestones

  • Phase 1: Quality & Testing - CI/CD, testing, coverage
  • Phase 2: Enhanced Input - Undo/redo, keybindings, history
  • Phase 3: Terminal Features - Colors, Unicode, mouse support
  • Phase 4: Platform & Extensibility - Windows, plugins, async
  • v1.0 Release - Documentation and stable release

See docs/ROADMAP.md for the complete roadmap.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please see docs/CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

Key areas where help is needed:

  • #3 - Integration tests
  • #10 - Syntax highlighting
  • #12 - Unicode support
  • #20 - API documentation

Documentation

  • Architecture Overview - Internal design
  • Contributing Guide - How to contribute
  • Roadmap - Development plans

License

Apache-2.0 License - See LICENSE file for details.

name: config
description: A comprehensive configuration management library for Zig 0.15.1. Supports YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, Properties formats with unified API, XDG compliance, hot-reload, async loading, remote config (etcd/Consul), secure secrets, validation with regex patterns, diff utilities, and provenance tracking.
readme_content:
zigconfig

A comprehensive configuration management library for Zig 0.16.0, inspired by Viper.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.0
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • Multi-format support - YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, Properties, Dotenv with unified API
  • Type-safe loading - Generic Loader with compile-time struct validation
  • XDG compliance - Respects XDG Base Directory Specification
  • Cross-platform - Native paths for Linux, macOS, and Windows
  • Precedence rules - override > flags > env > project > user > system > runtime_default > defaults
  • Secure secrets - File/stdin only, never flags/env (unlike Viper!)
  • Encrypted secrets - HashiCorp Vault and 1Password CLI providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and encrypted-file-at-rest are not currently supported)
  • Validation - Built-in validators for common patterns (email, URL, IPv4, port, etc.)
  • Provenance tracking - Know exactly where each value came from (unique to zigconfig)
  • Command-line flags - Full flag parsing with FlagParser
  • Hot-reload - File watching with automatic config refresh
  • Remote config - etcd v3 and Consul KV store support
  • Async loading - Parallel configuration file loading
  • Config diffing - Compare configurations and detect changes
  • Serialization - Export to JSON, YAML, TOML, or ENV format
  • Runtime overrides - Set() and SetDefault() for runtime configuration
  • Environment binding - BindEnv(), AutomaticEnv(), and key replacers
  • Key aliases - Register aliases for configuration keys
  • Case-insensitive access - Optional case-insensitive key matching

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .config = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/config/-/archive/main/config-main.tar.gz",
        // .hash = "...",  // Add after first fetch
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const config = b.dependency("config", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("config", config.module("config"));

Quick Start

Unified Value API

Parse any configuration format with a single API:

const config = @import("config");
const std = @import("std");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Parse any config file - format is auto-detected from extension
    var value = try config.parseFile(allocator, "config.yaml");
    defer value.deinit();

    // Access nested values with dot notation
    const host = value.getString("server.host") orelse "localhost";
    const port = value.getInt("server.port") orelse 8080;
    const debug = value.getBool("debug") orelse false;

    std.debug.print("Server: {s}:{d} (debug: {})\n", .{ host, port, debug });
}

Typed Configuration Loader

For type-safe configuration with defaults:

const config = @import("config");

const AppConfig = struct {
    host: []const u8 = "localhost",
    port: u16 = 8080,
    debug: bool = false,
};

pub fn main() !void {
    const allocator = std.heap.page_allocator;

    var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
    defer loader.deinit();

    const cfg = try loader.load(.{
        .app_name = "myapp",
        .filename = "config.toml",
        .env_prefix = "MYAPP_",
    });

    // cfg is now populated from all sources with proper precedence
}

API Reference

Configuration Parsing

// Parse from file (format auto-detected from extension)
pub fn parseFile(allocator: Allocator, path: []const u8) !Value;

// Parse from content with explicit format
pub fn parseContent(allocator: Allocator, content: []const u8, format: Format) !Value;

Value Access

pub const Value = struct {
    pub fn getString(self: Self, path: []const u8) ?[]const u8;
    pub fn getInt(self: Self, path: []const u8) ?i64;
    pub fn getFloat(self: Self, path: []const u8) ?f64;
    pub fn getBool(self: Self, path: []const u8) ?bool;
    pub fn has(self: Self, path: []const u8) bool;
    pub fn getList(self: Self, path: []const u8) ?[]Self;
    pub fn deinit(self: *Self) void;
};

XDG Directories

const xdg = config.xdg;

// Get XDG-compliant config directory for your app
const config_dir = try xdg.getConfigDir(allocator, "myapp");
// Returns: ~/.config/myapp (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/myapp)

const data_dir = try xdg.getDataDir(allocator, "myapp");
// Returns: ~/.local/share/myapp

const cache_dir = try xdg.getCacheDir(allocator, "myapp");
// Returns: ~/.cache/myapp

Secret Handling

const secret = config.secret;

// Read secrets only from files (never from flags/env!)
const password = try secret.readFromFile("/run/secrets/password", allocator);

// Or read from stdin (for interactive or piped input)
const token = try secret.readFromStdin(allocator);

// Safely redact for logging
std.debug.print("Password: {s}\n", .{secret.redact(password)});
// Output: Password: ***REDACTED***

// Securely zero memory when done
secret.secureZero(password);

Validation

const validate = config.validate;

// Validate configuration values
try validate.required(host);
try validate.minLength(password, 8);
try validate.maxLength(username, 64);
try validate.port(port);
try validate.hostname(host);
try validate.url(endpoint);
try validate.email(contact);
try validate.intRange(timeout, 1, 3600);
try validate.oneOf(log_level, &.{ "debug", "info", "warn", "error" });

Provenance Tracking

var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
defer loader.deinit();

_ = try loader.load(.{ .app_name = "myapp" });

// See where each value came from
const tracker = loader.getTracker();
if (tracker.get("port")) |tracked| {
    std.debug.print("port = {s} (from {s})\n", .{
        tracked.value,
        tracked.source.format(),
    });
}
// Output: port = 9000 (from env)

Dotenv Support

const dotenv = config.dotenv;

// Load .env file
const entries = try dotenv.load(".env", allocator);
defer allocator.free(entries);

for (entries) |entry| {
    std.debug.print("{s}={s}\n", .{ entry.key, entry.value });
}

Runtime Overrides

var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
defer loader.deinit();

// Set values with highest precedence (overrides everything)
try loader.set("port", "9000");
try loader.set("debug", "true");

// Set runtime defaults (lowest precedence, below struct defaults)
try loader.setDefault("host", "0.0.0.0");

const cfg = try loader.load(.{ .app_name = "myapp" });
// cfg.port == 9000 (from set())
// cfg.host == "0.0.0.0" (from setDefault(), if not set elsewhere)

Key Aliases

var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
defer loader.deinit();

// Register aliases - both "hostname" and "server" resolve to "host"
try loader.registerAlias("hostname", "host");
try loader.registerAlias("server", "host");

// Now setting "hostname" or "server" affects the "host" field
try loader.set("hostname", "myserver.local");

Case-Insensitive Keys

const cfg = try loader.load(.{
    .app_name = "myapp",
    .case_insensitive = true,  // Enable case-insensitive key matching
});
// Now HOST, Host, and host all match the "host" field

Environment Variable Binding

var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
defer loader.deinit();

// Explicit binding: "host" reads from DATABASE_HOST or SERVICE_HOST
try loader.bindEnv("host", &.{ "DATABASE_HOST", "SERVICE_HOST" });

// Single binding shorthand
try loader.bindEnvSingle("port", "SERVICE_PORT");

// Automatic env discovery with prefix
try loader.automaticEnv("MYAPP");
// Now MYAPP_HOST -> host, MYAPP_PORT -> port, etc.

// Custom key transformation
loader.setEnvKeyReplacer(.{
    .replacements = &.{
        .{ .from = ".", .to = "_" },  // server.host -> SERVER_HOST
        .{ .from = "-", .to = "_" },  // log-level -> LOG_LEVEL
    },
    .to_upper = true,
});

Value Checking

var loader = config.Loader(AppConfig).init(allocator);
defer loader.deinit();

try loader.set("port", "9000");
_ = try loader.load(.{ .app_name = "myapp" });

// Check if a key was explicitly set (via set() or loaded from sources)
if (loader.isSet("port")) {
    std.debug.print("port was explicitly configured\n", .{});
}

// Check if a key has any value (including defaults)
if (loader.has("host")) {
    const host = loader.get("host").?;
    std.debug.print("host = {s}\n", .{host});
}

Supported Formats

Format Extensions Description
YAML .yaml, .yml Full nested structures, lists, flow-style
JSON .json Standard JSON with nested objects
TOML .toml Section-based configuration
INI .ini Section-based INI configuration
Properties .properties Java properties format

Configuration Precedence

Values are loaded in this order (higher priority overrides lower):

Priority Source Description

1 Flags Command-line overrides
2 Environment PREFIX_FIELD env vars
3 Project ./config.toml
4 User ~/.config/APP/config.toml
5 System /etc/APP/config.toml
6 Runtime Default setDefault() calls
7 (lowest) Default Struct field default values

name: json
description: RFC 8259 compliant JSON parser and JSON Schema 2020-12 validator for Zig. Features normalized decimal number handling, full encoding/serialization support, and ECMA-262 regex pattern validation.
readme_content:
json

A fully RFC 8259 compliant JSON library for Zig 0.16.0 with JSON Schema 2020-12 validation.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.0+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • RFC 8259 Compliant Parsing - Strict JSON parsing with proper error handling
  • JSON Schema 2020-12 Validation - Full draft support with ECMA-262 regex
  • Type-Safe Encoding - Encode any Zig type to JSON with comptime reflection
  • Streaming Output - Writer-based API for memory-efficient encoding
  • Pretty Printing - Configurable indentation and formatting
  • Normalized Numbers - Exact decimal representation without floating-point errors
  • Unicode Support - Full UTF-8 and surrogate pair handling
  • Zero External Dependencies - Pure Zig implementation

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .json = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/json/-/archive/main/json-main.tar.gz",
        // Add hash after first fetch
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const json = b.dependency("json", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});

exe.root_module.addImport("json", json.module("json"));

Quick Start

Parse JSON

const std = @import("std");
const json = @import("json");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    const input =
        \\{"name": "json", "version": 1}
    ;

    var err = json.ParseError.init();
    var doc = try json.parse(allocator, input, .{}, &err);
    defer doc.deinit();

    // Access parsed values
    for (doc.root.obj) |member| {
        std.debug.print("{s}: ", .{member.k});
        switch (member.v) {
            .str => |s| std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{s}),
            .num => |n| std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{n.lexeme}),
            else => std.debug.print("...\n", .{}),
        }
    }
}

Encode Zig Types

const Point = struct { x: i32, y: i32 };
const point = Point{ .x = 10, .y = 20 };

// Minified output
const output = try json.encode(allocator, point, .{});
defer allocator.free(output);
// {"x":10,"y":20}

// Pretty printed
const pretty = try json.encode(allocator, point, .{ .indent = "  " });
defer allocator.free(pretty);
// {
//   "x": 10,
//   "y": 20
// }

Validate with JSON Schema

const schema_json =
    \\{
    \\  "type": "object",
    \\  "required": ["name"],
    \\  "properties": {
    \\    "name": {"type": "string"},
    \\    "age": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}
    \\  }
    \\}
;

var err = json.ParseError.init();

// Compile schema
var schema_doc = try json.parse(allocator, schema_json, .{}, &err);
defer schema_doc.deinit();

var compiled = try json.compileSchema(allocator, &schema_doc, .{}, null, &err);
defer compiled.deinit();

// Validate instance
var data_doc = try json.parse(allocator, "{\"name\": \"Alice\"}", .{}, &err);
defer data_doc.deinit();

const report = try json.validate(allocator, &compiled, data_doc.root, .{});
defer allocator.free(report.errors);

if (report.ok) {
    std.debug.print("Valid!\n", .{});
}

Documentation

  • Getting Started - Installation and first steps
  • API Reference - Complete API documentation
  • Examples - Usage patterns and recipes
  • Roadmap - Planned features and issue tracking

floats Number (NaN/Inf → null)
[]const u8 String
