name: toml
description: A fully compliant TOML v1.1.0 parser for Zig 0.15.2 with v1.0.0 compatibility mode. Features typed value tree output, version-gated parsing, comprehensive error handling, and zero external dependencies.
readme_content:
toml

A fully compliant TOML v1.1.0 parser for Zig 0.15.2 with v1.0.0 compatibility mode.

Supported TOML Versions

  • TOML v1.1.0 (default) - Full support including:
    • Inline tables with trailing commas and newlines
    • Local time with omitted seconds (assumes :00)
  • TOML v1.0.0 - Strict compatibility mode with v1.0 restrictions

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.15.2+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • Full TOML v1.1.0 compliance with typed value tree output
  • Version-gated parsing (v1.0.0 / v1.1.0)
  • toml-test compatible tagged JSON emitter with deterministic sorted keys
  • UTF-8 validation (rejects invalid UTF-8)
  • All TOML types: string, integer, float, bool, datetime, date, time, array, table
  • String escapes: \b \t \n \f \r \e \" \\ \x \u \U
  • Numbers with underscores and bases (hex, octal, binary)
  • Configurable limits: max_depth, max_bytes
  • Detailed error diagnostics with line/column location
  • Arena-based memory management

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .toml = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/toml/-/archive/main/toml-main.tar.gz",
        // .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const toml_dep = b.dependency("toml", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("toml", toml_dep.module("toml"));

API Usage

Basic Parsing

const toml = @import("toml");
const std = @import("std");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    const input =
        \\[server]
        \\host = "localhost"
        \\port = 8080
        \\
        \\[database]
        \\url = "postgres://localhost/db"
    ;

    const doc = try toml.parse(allocator, input, .{});
    defer doc.deinit();

    // Access values
    if (doc.root.get("server")) |server| {
        if (server.get("host")) |host| {
            std.debug.print("Host: {s}\n", .{host.string});
        }
        if (server.get("port")) |port| {
            std.debug.print("Port: {d}\n", .{port.integer});
        }
    }

    // Path-based lookup
    const path = &[_][]const u8{ "database", "url" };
    if (doc.getPath(path)) |url| {
        std.debug.print("DB URL: {s}\n", .{url.string});
    }
}

Parse with Error Handling

const result = toml.parseWithError(allocator, input, .{});
switch (result) {
    .ok => |*doc| {
        defer doc.deinit();
        // Use document...
    },
    .err => |e| {
        std.debug.print("Parse error at line {d}, column {d}: {s}\n", .{
            e.line, e.column, e.message,
        });
    },
}

Version Selection

// TOML v1.1.0 (default)
const doc = try toml.parse(allocator, input, .{ .version = .v1_1_0 });

// TOML v1.0.0 strict mode
const doc = try toml.parse(allocator, input, .{ .version = .v1_0_0 });

Tagged JSON Output (toml-test format)

const doc = try toml.parse(allocator, input, .{});
defer doc.deinit();

const stdout = std.io.getStdOut().writer();
try toml.writeTaggedJson(doc, stdout);

Limits

const doc = try toml.parse(allocator, input, .{
    .max_depth = 64,              // Maximum nesting depth (default: 128)
    .max_bytes = 1024 * 1024,     // Maximum input size (default: 16MB)
});

Parallel (Batch) API

For large fan-outs -- validating many config snippets in CI, lint passes over a directory tree, etc. -- toml.parallel exposes a batch entrypoint that runs across worker threads from a shared thread_pool-backed pool:

const toml = @import("toml");
var inputs: [32][]const u8 = undefined;
for (&inputs) |*s| s.* = "key = \"value\"";

var ctx = try toml.parallel.ParallelContext.initDefault(allocator);
defer ctx.deinit();

var results: [32]toml.parallel.ParseResult = undefined;
ctx.parseDocuments(&inputs, &results);
defer for (&results) |*r| if (r.doc) |d| d.deinit();

Every successful result carries the parsed Document; the caller owns deinit. See docs/API.md for the full contract.

CLI Usage

toml-test-decoder

A CLI binary for use with toml-test:

# Build
zig build

# Run decoder
echo 'a = 42' | ./zig-out/bin/toml-test-decoder
# Output: {"a":{"type":"integer","value":"42"}}

# Use with toml-test
toml-test ./zig-out/bin/toml-test-decoder
  • Reads TOML from stdin
  • On success: prints tagged JSON to stdout, exits 0
  • On failure: prints one-line diagnostic to stderr, exits 1

Public Types

pub const TomlVersion = enum { v1_0_0, v1_1_0 };

pub const ParseOptions = struct {
    version: TomlVersion = .v1_1_0,
    max_depth: u16 = 128,
    max_bytes: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024,
};

pub const ErrorCode = enum {
    InvalidUtf8,
    UnexpectedToken,
    InvalidEscape,
    InvalidUnicodeScalar,
    DuplicateKey,
    KeyRedefinesNonTable,
    TableRedefined,
    ArrayOfTablesConflict,
    InlineTableNewlineNotAllowed,
    InlineTableTrailingCommaNotAllowed,
    LocalTimeSecondsOmittedNotAllowed,
    LimitExceeded,
    // ...
};

pub const ParseError = struct {
    code: ErrorCode,
    byte_index: usize,
    line: u32,      // 1-based
    column: u32,    // 1-based (bytes, not graphemes)
    message: []const u8,
};

pub const ValueTag = enum {
    table, array, string, integer, float, bool,
    datetime, datetime_local, date_local, time_local,
};

pub const Value = union(ValueTag) { /* ... */ };

pub const Document = struct {
    pub fn deinit(self: *Document) void;
    pub fn getPath(self: *const Document, path: []const []const u8) ?*const Value;
};

pub fn parse(alloc: Allocator, input: []const u8, opts: ParseOptions) !*Document;
pub fn parseWithError(alloc: Allocator, input: []const u8, opts: ParseOptions) ParseResult;
pub fn writeTaggedJson(doc: *const Document, writer: anytype) !void;

Running Tests

# Verify Zig version
zig version  # must be 0.15.2

# Run all tests
zig build test

# Build CLI only
zig build

File Structure

/toml
  build.zig
  LICENSE
  README.md
  src/
    toml.zig           # Public API
    parser.zig         # TOML parser
    lexer.zig          # Tokenizer
    value.zig          # Value types and Document
    error.zig          # Error types
    json_tagged.zig    # Tagged JSON emitter
    bin/
      toml_test_decoder.zig  # CLI binary
  tests/
    accept.zig         # Acceptance tests

Design Rationale

  • Arena allocator: Document owns all memory via ArenaAllocator; single deinit() frees everything
  • Version gating: TomlVersion enum enables strict v1.0 or permissive v1.1 parsing at parse time
  • Deterministic JSON: Keys sorted lexicographically (byte order) at every level for reproducible output
  • Typed errors: ErrorCode enum + ParseError struct with exact byte/line/column for diagnostics
  • No external dependencies: Zig stdlib only; works on POSIX and Windows
  • Security first: UTF-8 validation, bounds checks, configurable depth/size limits, no panics on malformed input
  • Zero-copy where possible: String slices reference arena-allocated copies; path lookup without allocation

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE file for details.

name: yaml
description: A complete YAML 1.2.2 parser and emitter library for Zig 0.15.2. Features streaming event-based parser, document graph representation, schema-based resolution (failsafe/json/core), canonical emitter, and resource limits for DoS protection.
readme_content:
yaml

A complete YAML 1.2.2 parser and emitter library for Zig.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.15.1+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • Broad YAML 1.2.2 support: block/flow collections, anchors & aliases (with cycle detection), tags, multi-document streams, block scalars, and the failsafe/json/core/yaml11 schemas. Conformance against the official yaml-test-suite is wired into CI (zig build test-suite) and is being driven toward full coverage; see docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md for the tracked exceptions.
  • Streaming event-based parser (O(n) complexity)
  • Document graph representation with anchor/alias preservation at the graph layer (note: resolveToValue → dumpAll expands/inlines aliases)
  • Schema-based value resolution (failsafe, json, core, yaml11)
  • Canonical emitter with deterministic output
  • Zero external dependencies (stdlib only)
  • Resource limits for safety against DoS attacks (bounded depth, node count, alias expansion, scalar and input size)

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .yaml = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/yaml/-/archive/v0.1.1/yaml-v0.1.1.tar.gz",
        .hash = "yaml-0.1.1-lcW-hBqKBADGkeBKGWHbUCuOt6YOX_RCgK7hB0hw5jx0",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const yaml = b.dependency("yaml", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("yaml", yaml.module("yaml"));

Quick Start

const yaml = @import("yaml");
const std = @import("std");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    const input =
        \\---
        \\server:
        \\  host: localhost
        \\  port: 8080
        \\features:
        \\  - auth
        \\  - logging
    ;

    // Load documents
    var docs = try yaml.loadAll(allocator, input, .{});
    defer {
        for (docs) |*d| d.deinit();
        allocator.free(docs);
    }

    // Resolve to values
    for (docs) |*doc| {
        const value = try yaml.resolveToValue(allocator, doc, .{});
        // Use value...
    }
}

API Reference

Parser (Event-based)

pub const Parser = struct {
    pub fn init(a: Allocator, input: []const u8, o: ParseOptions) !Parser;
    pub fn nextEvent(self: *Parser) !Event;
    pub fn deinit(self: *Parser) void;
};

Document Graph

pub fn loadAll(a: Allocator, input: []const u8, o: ParseOptions) ![]Document;

pub const Document = struct {
    pub fn deinit(self: *Document) void;
    pub fn node(self: *const Document, id: NodeId) *const Node;
};

Value Resolution

pub fn resolveToValue(a: Allocator, doc: *const Document, o: ParseOptions) !Value;

pub const Value = union(enum) {
    null, bool: bool, int: i64, big_int: []const u8,
    float: f64, inf_pos, inf_neg, nan,
    str: []const u8, seq: []Value,
    map: []struct { k: Value, v: Value },
};

Emitter

pub fn dumpAll(a: Allocator, docs: []const Value, o: EmitOptions) ![]u8;

Options

pub const ParseOptions = struct {
    schema: Schema = .core,           // failsafe, json, core
    unique_keys: bool = true,
    max_bytes: usize = 8*1024*1024,   // 8 MiB
    max_depth: u16 = 200,
    max_nodes: u32 = 1_000_000,
    max_aliases: u32 = 5000,
    max_scalar_bytes: usize = 1024*1024,
};

Supported YAML Features

  • Multi-document streams (--- / ...)
  • Directives (%YAML, %TAG)
  • Tags (verbatim !<uri>, shorthand !!type, primary !tag)
  • Anchors (&name) and aliases (*name)
  • Block collections (sequences and mappings)
  • Flow collections ([...] and {...})
  • All scalar styles:
    • Plain
    • Single-quoted ('...')
    • Double-quoted ("..." with escape sequences)
    • Literal block (| with chomping indicators)
    • Folded block (> with chomping indicators)
  • Comments (ignored)

Testing

# Run all tests
zig build test

# Run unit tests only
zig build test-unit

# Run acceptance tests only
zig build test-accept

Design Rationale

  1. Layered architecture (scanner -> parser -> composer -> resolver) enables streaming, testability, and clear separation of concerns per YAML spec stages.

  2. O(n) streaming scan achieved by single-pass tokenization with indent stack tracking; no quadratic rescans for block scalar boundaries.

  3. Graph-first design preserves anchors/aliases in document representation, enabling round-trip fidelity and cycle detection during resolution.

  4. Schema resolution deferred to value layer allows same document graph to be interpreted under different schemas without re-parsing.

  5. Resource limits enforced early at scanner/parser level prevents DoS from deeply nested structures, large scalars, or alias bombs.

  6. Canonical emitter determinism via block-style output, sorted traversal order, and predictable escaping ensures reproducible serialization.

  7. No YAML 1.1 merge key (<<) processing avoids implicit data transformations that break security expectations in configuration files.

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE file for details.

name: dns
description: zigdns - A comprehensive DNS library for Zig with recursive resolution, caching, connection pooling, and the zdig CLI tool
readme_content:
zigdns - Zig DNS Library

A comprehensive pure Zig implementation of the Domain Name System (DNS) protocol. Supports both stub and recursive resolution with modern transport protocols.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.16.0+
Platforms Linux (primary); macOS/Windows not yet supported

Features

Implemented

  • RFC 1035 Compliant: Full DNS message parsing and encoding
  • Full Recursive Resolution: Iterative resolution from root servers
  • QNAME Minimization: RFC 7816 privacy-preserving queries
  • 0x20 Case Randomization: Cache poisoning protection
  • Stub Resolver: Simple forwarding to upstream DNS servers (UDP/TCP)
  • EDNS0 Support: Extended DNS with larger UDP payloads (RFC 6891)
  • Response Caching: TTL-aware LRU caching with negative caching (RFC 2308)
  • DoT Transport: DNS over TLS with pluggable TLS backend (RFC 7858)
  • DoH Transport: DNS over HTTPS with pluggable HTTP backend (RFC 8484)
  • DoQ Transport: DNS over QUIC with pluggable QUIC backend (RFC 9250)
  • Zone Transfers: Full AXFR/IXFR support (RFC 5936, RFC 1995)
  • Cache Protection: Bailiwick checking, TTL capping (RFC 5452)
  • Cache Prefetching: Proactive cache refresh before TTL expiration
  • DNSSEC Primitives: Ed25519, ECDSA P-256/P-384 signature verification, DS, NSEC/NSEC3 (RFC 4033/4034/4035). ⚠️ Not yet wired into resolution — the validator is never invoked and queries do not set the EDNS DO bit, so resolved answers are not DNSSEC-validated (#207).
  • EDNS Client Subnet: Geo-aware DNS queries (RFC 7871)
  • DNS Cookies: Lightweight transaction security (RFC 7873)
  • Linux: primary supported platform. macOS/Windows are not yet supported — the socket compatibility layer is currently Linux-only (#250).
  • Minimal Dependencies: Pure Zig implementation using the standard library (optional thread-pool dependency for parallelism)
  • Record Types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, SOA, TXT, DNAME, SRV, CAA, TLSA, SVCB, HTTPS, DNSKEY, RRSIG, DS, NSEC, NSEC3

Project Status

See ROADMAP.md and GitLab Issues for detailed status.

Phase Description Status
Phase 1 Core Recursion Complete
Phase 2 Production Ready (DoT, caching, zone transfers) Complete
Phase 3 DNSSEC Validation Primitives only — signature/DS/NSEC code exists but is not wired into resolution; answers are not validated (#207). RSA (8/10/5) pending.
Phase 4 Modern Features (DoH, DoQ, ECS, Cookies, Prefetch) Complete

Requirements

  • Zig 0.16.0 or later (the library uses the std.Io APIs introduced in 0.16)

Installation

Add dns as a dependency in your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .dns = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/dns/-/archive/main/dns-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const dns_dep = b.dependency("dns", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});

exe.root_module.addImport("dns", dns_dep.module("dns"));

Quick Start

Basic DNS Query (Stub Resolver)

const std = @import("std");
const dns = @import("dns");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const allocator = gpa.allocator();

    // Create a DNS client (uses system DNS servers by default)
    var client = try dns.Client.init(allocator);
    defer client.deinit();

    // Resolve a hostname
    var result = try client.resolveA("example.com");
    defer result.deinit(allocator);

    for (result.addresses) |addr| {
        std.debug.print("IP: {s}\n", .{addr});
    }
}

Custom DNS Server

var client = try dns.Client.initWithConfig(allocator, .{
    .servers = &[_][]const u8{ "8.8.8.8", "8.8.4.4" },
    .timeout_ms = 3000,
});

Low-Level Message Parsing

const dns = @import("dns");

// Parse a DNS response
const msg = try dns.Message.parse(response_bytes);

// Check if successful
if (msg.isSuccess()) {
    var iter = try msg.answers();
    while (try iter.next()) |rr| {
        if (rr.rtype == .a) {
            const ip = try rr.parseA();
            // Use ip[0..4] as IPv4 address bytes
        }
    }
}

Building

# Build the library
zig build

# Run all tests
zig build test --summary all

# Run specific test suites
zig build test-accept      # Acceptance tests
zig build test-util        # Utility module tests
zig build test-transport   # Transport tests
zig build test-resolver    # Resolver tests
zig build test-rfc1035     # RFC 1035 compliance
zig build test-rfc6891     # EDNS0 tests

# With optimization
zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseFast

Project Structure

src/
├── lib.zig              # Public API entry point
├── types.zig            # DNS types, enums, constants
├── name.zig             # DNS name handling, compression, 0x20
├── header.zig           # DNS header parsing/encoding
├── question.zig         # Question section handling
├── record.zig           # Resource record parsing (all types)
├── message.zig          # Complete message handling
├── edns.zig             # EDNS(0) OPT record, Client Subnet, Cookies
├── cache.zig            # Basic caching
├── stub.zig             # Stub resolver
├── recursive.zig        # Recursive resolver with QNAME min
├── client.zig           # High-level client API
├── resolver/            # Enhanced resolver components
│   ├── channel.zig      # Transport abstraction
│   ├── dns_cache.zig    # RFC 2308 negative caching
│   ├── cache_protection.zig  # RFC 5452 poisoning protection
│   ├── cache_prefetch.zig   # Proactive cache refresh
│   ├── zone_transfer.zig    # RFC 5936/1995 AXFR/IXFR
│   ├── dnssec.zig       # RFC 4033/4034/4035 DNSSEC validation
│   └── edns.zig         # EDNS handling
├── transports/          # Transport implementations
│   ├── udp.zig          # UDP transport
│   ├── tcp.zig          # TCP transport
│   ├── dot.zig          # DoT with TLS backend (RFC 7858)
│   ├── doh.zig          # DoH with HTTP backend (RFC 8484)
│   └── doq.zig          # DoQ with QUIC backend (RFC 9250)
└── util/                # Utilities
    ├── clock.zig        # Mockable clock
    ├── random.zig       # Mockable RNG
    ├── lru.zig          # LRU cache
    └── metrics.zig      # Prometheus metrics

Documentation

  • Architecture - System design and module overview
  • Roadmap - Implementation status and GitLab issues
  • RFC Compliance - RFC implementation status

Cross-Compilation

Zig's cross-compilation support allows building for any target:

# Linux ARM64
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu

# Windows x64
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows-msvc

# macOS ARM64
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos

# RISC-V 64
zig build -Dtarget=riscv64-linux-gnu

Contributing

See GitLab Issues for open tasks.

  1. Code passes zig fmt
  2. All tests pass
  3. New features include tests
  4. RFC compliance is maintained

RFC References

RFC Description Status
RFC 1034 Domain Names - Concepts Complete
RFC 1035 Domain Names - Implementation Complete
RFC 2308 Negative Caching Complete
RFC 3596 IPv6 (AAAA) Complete
RFC 4033 DNSSEC Introduction Partial**
RFC 4034 DNSSEC Resource Records Partial**
RFC 4035 DNSSEC Protocol Partial**
RFC 5155 NSEC3 Complete
RFC 6891 EDNS(0) Complete
RFC 7816 QNAME Minimization Complete
RFC 7858 DNS over TLS Complete***
RFC 7871 Client Subnet Complete
RFC 7873 DNS Cookies Complete
RFC 8484 DNS over HTTPS Complete*
RFC 9250 DNS over QUIC Complete*

* Requires external HTTP/QUIC library via pluggable backend interface

** Ed25519 and ECDSA (P-256/P-384) signature verification is implemented; RSA signature verification is not yet implemented

*** DoT transport interface exists with pluggable TLS backend; a TLS implementation must be provided by the consumer

Observability

This library ships an optional OpenTelemetry seam, gated behind -Dwith_otel=<bool> (default false).

When -Dwith_otel=false (the default) the seam collapses to a comptime-known no-op: every public helper in dns.observability returns a zero-sized Span{}, the otel dependency is never resolved, and the produced artifact contains zero otel symbols (verified by otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh).

When -Dwith_otel=true, the resolver emits one client-kind span per DNS query at every public entry point — Client.resolve, Client.lookupMX, StubResolver.resolveClass, and RecursiveResolver.resolve. Each span is named "DNS {qtype} {qname}" and carries the standard semantic-convention attributes:

  • dns.question.name
  • dns.question.type
  • network.protocol.name = "dns"

Bootstrap from your application entry point:

const std = @import("std");
const dns = @import("dns");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa: std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}) = .{};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();

    var otel = try dns.observability_init.Otel.init(gpa.allocator(), "my-app");
    otel.installGlobals();
    defer otel.deinit();

    var client = try dns.Client.init(gpa.allocator());
    defer client.deinit();
    _ = try client.resolve("example.com", .a); // emits a span
}

Configuration follows the OpenTelemetry environment-variable contract (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, etc). Defaults: parentbased_traceidratio @ 5%, OTLP/HTTP to http://localhost:4318.

See otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md for the full recipe.

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE for details.

name: cli
description: A comprehensive CLI framework for Zig with command parsing, shell completions (bash/zsh/fish), configuration loading (TOML/JSON/YAML), and terminal utilities
readme_content:
cli

A comprehensive command-line interface and configuration library for Zig, providing Cobra/Viper-class features for building production-quality CLI applications.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.15.2+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

CLI Features

  • Nested command trees with subcommands and aliases
  • Type-safe flag parsing (bool, int, float, string, path, string_array)
  • Automatic help generation with examples-first approach
  • Shell completion generation (bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell)
  • Man page generation in roff format
  • Typo-suggestion helpers (Levenshtein distance) for building "did you mean" error messages
  • Signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM) with cleanup callbacks
  • Pre/post-run hooks for command lifecycle management
  • Default flag values applied when unspecified

Config Features

  • Multiple format support (TOML, JSON, YAML) via config
  • XDG Base Directory compliance (~/.config, /etc)
  • Strict precedence: flags > env > project > user > system > defaults
  • Secret handling: file/stdin only, never flags/env
  • Provenance tracking for debugging configuration sources
  • Validation hooks

Terminal Features

  • TTY detection and terminal size
  • ANSI color with NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb compliance
  • Pager integration (less) for long output
  • Progress indicators (spinners, bars) - TTY-aware
  • Interactive prompts (input, password, confirm, select, multi-select)

Installation

Add to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .cli = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/cli/-/archive/main/cli-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...", // Run `zig fetch` to get the hash
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const cli_dep = b.dependency("cli", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("cli", cli_dep.module("cli"));
exe.root_module.addImport("config", cli_dep.module("config"));

Quick Start

const std = @import("std");
const cli = @import("cli");

const root_cmd = cli.Command{
    .name = "myapp",
    .summary = "My application",
    .examples = &.{
        "myapp serve --port=8080",
        "myapp config show",
    },
    .flags = &.{
        cli.FlagSpec{
            .name = "verbose",
            .short = 'v',
            .help = "Enable verbose output",
            .ftype = .bool,
        },
    },
    .run = myRun,
};

fn myRun(ctx: *cli.Context) !void {
    if (ctx.getBool("verbose")) {
        try ctx.print("Verbose mode enabled\n", .{});
    }
    try ctx.print("Hello, World!\n", .{});
}

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();

    const args = try std.process.argsAlloc(gpa.allocator());
    defer std.process.argsFree(gpa.allocator(), args);

    const exit_code = try cli.run(&root_cmd, args, gpa.allocator());
    std.process.exit(exit_code);
}

Configuration Loading

const config = @import("config");

const AppConfig = struct {
    host: []const u8 = "localhost",
    port: u16 = 8080,
    debug: bool = false,
};

// Loads from (in order): flags > env > project (./) > user (~/.config) > system (/etc)
const cfg = try config.load(AppConfig, .{
    .app_name = "myapp",
    .filename = "config.toml",
    .env_prefix = "MYAPP_",
});

Configuration Precedence

+--------+  highest priority
| Flags  |  --port=7000
+--------+
    |
+--------+
|  Env   |  MYAPP_PORT=8000
+--------+
    |
+--------+
|Project |  ./config.toml, ./.env
+--------+
    |
+--------+
| User   |  ~/.config/myapp/config.toml
+--------+
    |
+--------+
| System |  /etc/myapp/config.toml
+--------+
    |
+--------+  lowest priority
|Default |  struct field defaults
+--------+

Testing

# Unit tests
zig build test

# Integration tests
zig build test-integration

Security Notes

Secrets Must Never Be in Flags or Environment Variables

// WRONG: This will be rejected
myapp --token=secret123

// CORRECT: Use file
myapp --token-file=/path/to/token

// CORRECT: Pipe via stdin
cat token.txt | myapp login

Configure secret flags:

cli.FlagSpec{
    .name = "token",
    .help = "Auth token (use --token-file instead)",
    .ftype = .string,
    .secret = .from_file_or_stdin,  // Rejects --token=...
},
cli.FlagSpec{
    .name = "token-file",
    .help = "Path to file containing token",
    .ftype = .path,
},

Error Message Redaction

Paths to sensitive files are automatically redacted in error messages:

  • /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd
  • .ssh/, .gnupg/, .aws/
  • Files named credentials, secrets, .env

Color and TTY Behavior

Condition Color Output
Not a TTY Disabled
--no-color flag Disabled
NO_COLOR env set Disabled
TERM=dumb Disabled
Otherwise Enabled

Progress indicators and animations are automatically disabled when not a TTY.

Generating Completions

# Bash
myapp completion --shell bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/myapp

# Zsh
myapp completion --shell zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_myapp

# Fish
myapp completion --shell fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/myapp.fish

# PowerShell
myapp completion --shell powershell > myapp.ps1

Generating Man Pages

myapp man > /usr/local/share/man/man1/myapp.1

Output Modes

Flag Description
--json Machine-readable JSON output
--plain Plain text, one record per line
-q, --quiet Suppress non-essential output
--no-color Disable ANSI color codes
-n, --dry-run Show what would happen

Building

# Build
zig build

# Run tests
zig build test

# Run demo
zig build run -- --help

# Build with optimizations
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe

Cross-Platform Support

Platform Architecture Status
Linux x86_64 Native
Linux ARM64 Native
Linux ARM Cross-compile
Linux RISC-V Cross-compile
macOS ARM64 (M1/M2) Native
macOS x86_64 Cross-compile
Windows x86_64 Native
Windows ARM64 Cross-compile

Documentation

  • Getting Started - Quick start guide
  • Architecture - Design overview and module structure
  • API Reference - Public API documentation
  • Roadmap - Planned features and Cobra comparison

Guides

  • Subcommands - Nested command structures
  • Config Precedence - Configuration loading order
  • Shell Completions - Completion script generation
  • Cross-Platform - Platform-specific notes
  • Testing - Testing guide

Project Status

This library is under active development. See the Roadmap for a complete Cobra feature comparison.

Planned

Issue Description
#12 Publish to Zig package registry

Recently Completed

  • PowerShell completion generation (#13)
  • Persistent hooks (PersistentPreRun/PostRun) (#14)
  • Flag groups (mutually exclusive/required together) (#16)
  • Positional argument validators (#17)
  • Flag value completion support (#22)
  • String array flag parsing (#1)
  • Signal handling (#3)
  • Interactive prompts (#7)
  • Progress indicators (#10)

Design Rationale

  1. Human-first defaults - Help, examples, and concise messaging + composability (stdout/JSON/--plain)
  2. Strict precedence & XDG compliance - Predictable configuration behavior
  3. Safety by default - Explicit aliases only, confirmations for destructive ops, no secrets in flags/env
  4. Clear separation of concerns - cli/, config/, term/, util/
  5. Deterministic builds - Pinned Zig version, no vendored dependencies, no network at build time
  6. TTY-aware UX - Progress/pager/color only when appropriate
  7. Machine-readable output - --json for tooling integration

Requirements

  • Zig 0.15.2 or compatible

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE

name: slog
description: slogz - A high-performance structured logging library for Zig, inspired by Go's slog. Features text/JSON handlers, async buffering, network sinks (TCP/UDP/HTTP), syslog RFC5424 support, and secret redaction.
readme_content:
slog

A high-performance structured logging library for Zig, inspired by Go's slog.

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.14.0+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Features

  • Multiple Output Handlers

    • Text handler (human-readable format)
    • JSON handler (structured JSON output)
    • Syslog RFC5424 handler
    • Rotating file handler with size-based rotation
    • Discard handler (for benchmarking)

  • Async Handler

    • Background thread delivery
    • Bounded queue with configurable size
    • Drop-oldest policy with metrics tracking
    • Optional blocking mode with timeout

  • Network Sinks

    • TCP with automatic reconnection and retry/backoff
    • UDP (fire-and-forget)
    • HTTP POST with configurable retry

  • Platform-Specific Handlers (feature-gated)

    • Journald (Linux, requires libsystemd)
    • Windows Event Log

  • Additional Features

    • Prometheus-style metrics export
    • i18n catalog for message translation
    • Secret redaction (sensitive values never logged)
    • Key sanitization for structured output
    • Zero-allocation for disabled/simple log calls
    • Stable key order in output

Installation

Add slog to your build.zig.zon:

.dependencies = .{
    .slog = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/slog/-/archive/main/slog-main.tar.gz",
        .hash = "...",
    },
},

Then in your build.zig:

const slog_dep = b.dependency("slog", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
exe.root_module.addImport("slog", slog_dep.module("slog"));

Quick Start

const std = @import("std");
const slog = @import("slog");

pub fn main() !void {
    // Create a text handler writing to stderr
    var ctx = slog.text.Context.init(
        std.io.getStdErr().writer().any(),
        .info,
        slog.Clock.system(),
    );
    const handler = slog.text.init(&ctx);

    // Create a logger
    const logger = slog.Logger.init(handler, .info, slog.Clock.system())
        .named("myapp");

    // Log messages
    try logger.info("app.started", &.{
        slog.Attr.string("version", "1.0.0"),
        slog.Attr.int("port", 8080),
    });
}

Output:

2025-01-02T03:04:05.000000Z INFO myapp app.started version=1.0.0 port=8080

Handlers

Text Handler

Human-readable log format:

var ctx = slog.text.Context.init(writer.any(), .info, slog.Clock.system());
const handler = slog.text.init(&ctx);

JSON Handler

Structured JSON output with stable key order:

var ctx = slog.json.Context.init(writer.any(), .info, slog.Clock.system());
const handler = slog.json.init(&ctx);

Output:

{"time":"2025-01-02T03:04:05.000000Z","level":"INFO","msg":"app.started","logger":"myapp","attrs":{"port":8080}}

Rotating File Handler

Size-based rotation with backup management:

var ctx = try slog.rotating_file.Context.init(allocator, .{
    .path = "/var/log/myapp.log",
    .max_bytes = 10 * 1024 * 1024,  // 10MB
    .max_backups = 5,
    .max_age_days = 30,
}, .info, slog.Clock.system());
defer ctx.deinit();

const handler = slog.rotating_file.init(&ctx);

Async Handler

Background thread delivery with bounded queue:

var async_ctx = try slog.async_handler.Context.init(allocator, .{
    .inner = inner_handler,
    .queue_size = 1024,
    .drop_oldest = true,
    .block_timeout_ms = 0,
});
defer async_ctx.deinit();

const handler = slog.async_handler.init(&async_ctx);

Syslog RFC5424

var ctx = slog.syslog.Context.init(writer.any(), .info, slog.Clock.system(), .{
    .facility = .local0,
    .hostname = "myhost",
    .app_name = "myapp",
    .procid = 1234,
});
const handler = slog.syslog.init(&ctx);

Output:

<134>1 2025-01-02T03:04:05.000000Z myhost myapp 1234 app.started [attrs@32473 port="8080"] Application started

Attribute Types

const attrs = &.{
    slog.Attr.string("user", "alice"),
    slog.Attr.int("count", 42),
    slog.Attr.uint("size", 1024),
    slog.Attr.float("ratio", 0.95),
    slog.Attr.boolean("enabled", true),
    slog.Attr.err("error", error.NotFound),
    slog.Attr.secret("api_key", "sk-xxx"),  // Redacted in output
};

Secret Redaction

Sensitive values marked with Attr.secret() are automatically redacted:

try logger.info("auth", &.{
    slog.Attr.string("user", "alice"),
    slog.Attr.secret("password", "hunter2"),  // Outputs: password=[REDACTED]
});

Log Levels

Level Value Description
trace -8 Fine-grained debugging
debug -4 Debugging information
info 0 Normal operational messages
warn 4 Warning conditions
error 8 Error conditions
fatal 12 Fatal errors (triggers fatal_hook)

Metrics

Export Prometheus-style metrics:

var buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
const output = slog.exportPrometheusMetrics(&buf);
std.debug.print("{s}", .{output});

Output:

# HELP slogz_logs_emitted_total Total number of log records emitted.
# TYPE slogz_logs_emitted_total counter
slogz_logs_emitted_total 1234
# HELP slogz_logs_dropped_total Total number of log records dropped.
# TYPE slogz_logs_dropped_total counter
slogz_logs_dropped_total 0
...

i18n Support

const json =
    \\{
    \\  "es": { "app.started": "aplicacion iniciada" },
    \\  "de": { "app.started": "Anwendung gestartet" }
    \\}
;

var catalog = try slog.i18n.Catalog.fromJson(allocator, json);
defer catalog.deinit();

const logger = base_logger.withTranslator("es", catalog.translator());
try logger.info("app.started", &.{});  // Logs "aplicacion iniciada"

Parallel Operations

The parallel operations module provides high-performance concurrent processing for logging operations including batch record formatting, multi-handler dispatch, and parallel sink writes. Each operation automatically falls back to sequential execution below a configurable threshold, so there is no overhead for small workloads.

const slog = @import("slog");
const parallel = slog.parallel;

// Format multiple log records in parallel (uses parallelism for 8+ records)
var inputs: [16]parallel.RecordInput = undefined;
var buffers: [16][]u8 = undefined;
var results: [16]parallel.FormattedRecord = undefined;

for (&buffers) |*buf| {
    buf.* = allocator.alloc(u8, 1024) catch unreachable;
}

for (&inputs) |*input| {
    input.* = .{
        .time_utc_us = 0,
        .level = 2,
        .message = "hello world",
        .logger = "myapp",
        .attrs_json = "{}",
    };
}

parallel.parallelRecordFormat(&inputs, &buffers, &results, myFormatter);

// Dispatch a record to multiple handlers in parallel (2+ handlers)
parallel.parallelHandlerDispatch(&handlers, record_data, &dispatch_results);

Parallel operations require the spice dependency for thread pool management. It is enabled by default and can be toggled with -Dspice=true or -Dspice=false at build time.

Feature Flags

Journald (Linux)

zig build -Dfeature_journald=true

Windows Event Log

zig build -Dfeature_windows_eventlog=true

Observability

slog carries an opt-in OpenTelemetry seam exposed at slogz.observability (and a bootstrap helper at slogz.observability_init). It is off by default; building or depending on slog without any extra flags emits zero otel/observability symbols and never resolves the otel package.

To compile in the seam:

zig build test -Dwith_otel=true
# or, when consuming slog as a dependency:
zig build -Dwith_otel=true

When the flag is on, the otel package is fetched lazily from the pinned SHA in build.zig.zon (.otel). When it is off, the verifier otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh confirms no otel/observability symbols leak into slog's static link.

slog is build-flag-only — the seam scaffolding exists for forward compatibility; slog itself does not emit spans (would create logging-feedback loops). Specifically:

  • slog is otel's transitive std.log backend (otel routes its internal diagnostic logs through slog when built with -Dotel_use_devnw_slog=true). If slog's log path emitted spans, those spans would call into otel, which logs through slog, which would emit more spans — an unbounded recursion.
  • The lazy = true dependency entry plus the comptime if (with_otel) gate in build.zig keep the cycle broken: a default-flag slog build never resolves the otel package, so otel can depend on slog without the dependency closing into a loop.

The seam is exposed for two reasons:

  1. Forward compatibility: a future slog operation that genuinely warrants a span (one that does not run inside the log-emission hot path) can call into the seam without re-plumbing the package manifest, build flags, or symbols.
  2. Consumer wiring: applications that embed slog inside an OpenTelemetry-aware service can use slogz.observability to instrument their own slog interactions with the same conventions and helpers the rest of the devnw/zig stack uses, and can use slogz.observability_init.Otel.init(...) from their main to bootstrap providers from OTEL_* env vars.

See src/observability.zig for the seam surface and src/observability_init.zig for the bootstrap helper. The integration recipe lives at otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md in the otel repository.

Building

# Build
zig build

# Run tests
zig build test

# Format code
zig build fmt

# Check for errors
zig build check

Performance

  • Zero allocations for disabled log levels
  • Lock-free metrics counters
  • Bounded async queue with configurable drop policy
  • Minimal overhead for simple log calls

Roadmap

Development is tracked via GitLab Issues.

Current Milestones

Phase Focus Status
Phase 1 Foundation - code quality, deprecated API removal Active
Phase 2 Platform Handlers - Windows Event Log, journald Planned
Phase 3 Network Sinks - TLS/HTTPS, DNS, attributes Planned
Phase 4 Advanced Features - multi-handler, sampling Planned
Phase 5 Testing & Documentation Planned

Key Upcoming Features

  • TLS/HTTPS support for HTTP sink
  • DNS hostname resolution
  • Multi-handler fan-out
  • Log sampling and rate limiting

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE for details.

name: ebnf
description: Zig EBNF grammar parser and code generator - generates recursive-descent parsers from EBNF specifications
readme_content:
zig-ebnfgen (Zig 0.15.1)

A tiny EBNF-to-Zig code generator plus an AST interpreter/CLI. It parses an EBNF grammar and either:

  • recognizes input strings with an in-process interpreter, or
  • generates a self-contained Zig module with a longest-match lexer and recursive-descent parser (ordered choice, greedy repetition, backtracking with lookahead).

The dialect follows the four control forms (sequence, choice, option, repetition) and the ::= assignment per the reference chapter’s Table 1.1 and examples (digit, integer, integer set). [Source: Chapter “EBNF: A Notation to Describe Syntax”.]

Requirements

  • Zig 0.15.1 (required)
  • Linux: Kernel 5.0+
  • macOS: 11.0+ (Big Sur or newer)
  • Windows: Windows 10+

Note: Older systems (e.g., Linux kernel 4.x) are not supported. See TROUBLESHOOTING.md for details.

Install & Build

Install Zig 0.15.1

# Using the provided script:
./scripts/install-zig.sh

# Or download manually from:
# https://ziglang.org/download/0.15.1/

# Verify installation:
zig version              # must print 0.15.1

Build & Test

zig build                # build CLI executable
zig build test           # run unit tests
./scripts/acceptance.sh  # run black-box CLI acceptance tests
zig build bench          # build benchmark executable
zig build run-bench      # run benchmarks

CLI

zig-ebnf generate  --in \<grammar.ebnf\> --out \<dir\> --start \<rule\> [--module-name \<name\>] [--backend rd|stub] [--permissive] [--emit-cli-demo]
zig-ebnf recognize --grammar \<grammar.ebnf\> --start \<rule\> --input \<str\>
zig-ebnf version
  • generate: validates grammar, emits Zig module files under --out/<module-name>/ (backend rd = recursive descent, stub = placeholder). Use --emit-cli-demo to include a small cli_demo.zig showcasing recognizer invocation.
  • recognize: runs an interpreter over the AST; on success prints
ACCEPT <rule> "<input>"

on failure prints

REJECT <rule> "<input>": <reason> @<index>

Errors (fail closed): SyntaxError, UndefinedSymbol, DuplicateRule, LeftRecursion, EmptyRepetition, UnreachableRule, AmbiguousChoice, IoError.

Permissive Mode

Pass --permissive (or use parseEbnfOpts(..., .{ .permissive = true })) to relax the lexer for ingesting large / mixed‑dialect grammars:

  • Falls back to treating otherwise unknown single characters as 1‑byte literal terminals.
  • Accepts all‑uppercase identifiers (FOO), mirroring some external specs.
  • Still performs duplicate / undefined symbol validation; i.e. structural correctness is enforced even when tokenization is lenient.

Use this only for bootstrapping foreign grammars; prefer strict mode for deterministic builds.

Undefined Symbol Diagnostics with Spans

Early validation records up to 8 undefined nonterminal references together with their source spans (line/column). The CLI re‑parses after an UndefinedSymbol error to report a concise multi‑line diagnostic:

Undefined symbols (first 8):
    missing_rule @ line X col Y
    other_missing @ line A col B

The span collection is O(refs) during parsing (no deep AST walk) by recording identifier occurrences inline.

Memory Model & Allocation

  • Expression graph (Expr nodes) lives in a single arena (std.heap.ArenaAllocator) owned by the AST.
  • Rule array, literal value slices, and diagnostic arrays use the caller allocator directly.
  • All literal terminal strings are owned by the AST and freed in AST.deinit().
  • Identifier occurrence table (for diagnostics) is arena‑allocated and thus bulk‑freed with the arena.

Literal Interning / Deduplication

The lexer now interns literal value slices (non‑empty) to avoid allocating duplicate copies for repeated punctuation or short tokens. During tokenization only the first occurrence of a distinct literal is retained in the AST’s literals list; subsequent identical lexemes reuse the canonical slice. Benefits:

  • Fewer heap allocations & frees for large grammars with many repeated operators.
  • Smaller working set (unique literal storage only).
  • No observable semantic change—slices remain immutable.

Interning deliberately skips the empty literal ("") which denotes the empty symbol.

Library API

pub const Error = error{
    SyntaxError, UndefinedSymbol, DuplicateRule, LeftRecursion,
    EmptyRepetition, UnreachableRule, AmbiguousChoice, IoError,
};

pub const GenBackend = enum { RecursiveDescent, Stub };
pub const GenOptions = struct {
    backend: GenBackend = .RecursiveDescent,
    module_name: []const u8 = "generated",
    start_rule: []const u8, // required
    emit_cli_demo: bool = false,
};

pub const Generated = struct {
    files: []const GeneratedFile,
};
pub const GeneratedFile = struct {
    path: []const u8,
    contents: []const u8,
};

pub fn parseEbnf(alloc: std.mem.Allocator, src: []const u8) !AST;
pub fn generateZig(alloc: std.mem.Allocator, ast: *const AST, opts: GenOptions) !Generated;

EBNF Dialect

  • Assignment: ::= (also accepts ⇐)
  • Alternation: |
  • Option: [ ... ]
  • Repetition: { ... } (greedy; reject if body can match empty)
  • Sequence: whitespace-separated
  • LHS names: [a-z][a-z0-9_]*
  • Terminals: '...' or "..."; escapes: \\, \", \', \n, \r, \t, \xHH
  • Empty: "" means the empty symbol
  • Comments: // to EOL and /* ... */ (nested ok)
  • Whitespace ignored between tokens unless some terminal includes whitespace (then it’s tokenized)

Semantics

  • Choice: ordered (left-first)
  • Option: try once; on failure succeed without consuming
  • Repetition: greedy; must make progress; fails grammar validation if body can match empty
  • Left recursion: detected (direct/indirect) and rejected at generation time
  • Lexer: tokens derived from terminals; longest-match; breaks ties by first-seen terminal order; whitespace skipped unless explicitly tokenized

Examples

See examples/integer.ebnf and examples/integer_set.ebnf. Try:

zig build run -- generate --in examples/integer.ebnf --out zig-out/gen/integer --start integer --module-name integer_gen

zig build run -- recognize --grammar examples/integer.ebnf --start integer --input "+142"
# ACCEPT integer "+142"

Security & Limits

  • No external deps; no path traversal: outputs restricted to --out/<module-name>/.
  • Memory budget ~512 MiB. ~200-rule grammars parse <2s on typical x86_64.
  • Deterministic codegen and stable token order.

Backends

Backend selection (flag: --backend rd|stub):

Backend Description Typical Use
rd Full recursive-descent parser + longest-match lexer Normal generation / integration
stub Minimal placeholder; rules fail, recognizer only checks empty Fast structural diffing, benchmarking codegen path

The stub backend shares the same header/meta generation; it’s intentionally tiny and not for recognition.

Implementation Status

See IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md for a comprehensive overview of all implemented features, test coverage, and known limitations.

ISO BNF module (bnf)

src/bnf/bnf.zig (exported as ebnf.bnf) is a second, independent parser for the ISO/IEC-standard "BNF" notation used by documents like ISO/IEC 39075 (GQL) — as opposed to the EBNF dialect the rest of this package targets. It handles that notation's conventions directly: column-0 <rule name> ::= headers, |-separated alternatives, [ ] optional groups, { } groups, postfix ... repetition, ALL_CAPS reserved-word terminals, single character literals, raw multi-character symbol/punctuation literals (e.g. ::, <-[, <>, ||), and !! See the Syntax Rules. implementation-defined markers.

const ebnf = @import("ebnf");
const bnf = ebnf.bnf;

var g = try bnf.parse(gpa, source_text);
defer g.deinit();

// Fails with error.UndefinedNonterminal if any `<...>` reference has no
// matching rule definition anywhere in the grammar.
try g.validate(gpa);

// Every ALL-CAPS reserved-word terminal referenced anywhere, deduplicated.
var kw = try g.keywords(gpa);
defer kw.deinit(gpa);

// Deep-copies every rule from `other` into `self` (e.g. layering a
// supplementary/vendor grammar extension on top of a base standard).
try g.mergeFrom(gpa, &other_grammar);

src/bnf/gen.zig (bnf.gen) generates deterministic or randomized sample sentences from a parsed Grammar:

var prng = std.Random.DefaultPrng.init(seed);
var cs = bnf.gen.ChoiceSource{ .prng = &prng };
const sentence = try bnf.gen.generate(gpa, &g, .{ .start = "GQL-program", .max_depth = 40 }, &cs);
defer gpa.free(sentence);

ChoiceSource can instead wrap a raw []const u8 byte buffer (.bytes), letting a fuzzer's input drive every choice/optional/repetition decision directly. Generation is termination-hardened against unit-production cycles and escape-less recursive rules: it always produces a finite sentence (or returns error.NoFiniteDerivation up front if the start rule truly has none), falling back to each region's minimal-cost derivation once a configurable max_depth/max_len budget is exceeded.

This module is exercised end-to-end against the real, unmodified ISO/IEC 39075 GQL BNF artifact vendored at testdata/ISO_IEC_39075.bnf.txt — see the "bnf: parses the full ISO/IEC 39075 GQL artifact" test in src/bnf/bnf.zig.

License

MIT

name: quic
description: High-performance QUIC protocol implementation in Zig. RFC 9000/9001/9002 compliant with TLS 1.3, HTTP/3 support, and cross-platform compatibility (Linux, macOS, Windows).
readme_content:
QUIC

Zig QUIC v1/v2 implementation (Zig 0.15.1+). Beta transport with comprehensive feature support. Requires OpenSSL for TLS 1.3 cryptographic operations at link time.

🎆 Implementation Highlights

  • Full QUIC v1 & v2 support with RFC 9000/9001/9002 compliance
  • 0-RTT early data transmission and reception
  • Session resumption with PSK (Pre-Shared Keys)
  • Connection migration with PATH_CHALLENGE/RESPONSE
  • Preferred address handling for server migration
  • Comprehensive test suite passing
  • Interoperability tested against 18 QUIC implementations

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Beta
Zig Version 0.15.1+
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Core Features

  • ✅ Transport: All frame types, connection ID management, path validation
  • ✅ Crypto: AES-128-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, header protection
  • ✅ TLS 1.3: Full integration with key derivation, PSK, 0-RTT
  • ✅ Signatures: ECDSA (P-256/P-384), RSA-PSS, Ed25519 (via external TLS dependency)
  • ✅ Recovery: Loss detection, PTO, congestion control (NewReno/CUBIC)
  • ✅ Flow Control: Connection and stream-level with dynamic limits
  • ✅ Migration: NAT rebinding, path validation, preferred address
  • ✅ Version Negotiation: QUIC v1 and v2, compatible VN
  • ✅ Streams: Multi-stream support with proper lifecycle management

Build

  • Debug: zig build
  • Release-safe: zig build -Drelease-safe=true

Tools

  • Build tools: zig build tools
  • Varint encode: ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint encode 64 → 40 40
  • Varint decode: ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint decode 7f ff → 16383
  • Varint underflow: ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint decode 40 prints VARINT_UNDERFLOW to stderr, exit 2

Tests

  • All tests: zig build test
  • Filtered TLS KAT only: zig build -Dtest-filter=tls_key_schedule_kat test
  • Short-header 1-RTT roundtrip is included in default test run.

Interoperability Testing

Test against other QUIC implementations:

  • Quick verification: ./scripts/interop_test.sh
  • Core tests: ./scripts/interop_verify.sh
  • Full matrix: ./scripts/interop_full.sh quick
  • Official run-profile replay: ./scripts/interop_runner_replay.sh --run-url "https://interop.seemann.io/?run=2026-02-16T09:04" --client zig,quic-go --server zig,quic-go

See examples/interop/README.md for detailed interop testing documentation.

Acceptance tests (exact outputs)

  • Cmd 1:
    • Run: zig build tools && ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint encode 64
    • Expect stdout: 40 40
    • Exit: 0
  • Cmd 2:
    • Run: ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint decode 7f ff
    • Expect stdout: 16383
    • Exit: 0
  • Cmd 3:
    • Run: ./zig-out/bin/quic-varint decode 40
    • Expect stderr contains: VARINT_UNDERFLOW
    • Exit: 2
  • Cmd 4:
    • Run: zig build test --test-filter "tls_key_schedule_kat"
    • Expect stdout contains: PASSED tls_key_schedule_kat
    • Exit: 0

CLI

  • Server: ./zig-out/bin/quic-server --bind 0.0.0.0:4433 --alpn h3 --datagram=true --compatible-vn --retry true --token-expiry-ms 60000
  • Client: ./zig-out/bin/quic-client --connect 127.0.0.1:4433 --sni test.local --alpn h3 --datagram=true --compatible-vn

With datagram enabled, the server will echo any DATAGRAM payloads. When --retry true is set, the server will issue a QUIC Retry with a stateless token bound to the client address; the client will re-send Initial with the token.

Docs

  • Gap analysis: docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md
  • Performance targets and benchmark gates: docs/PERFORMANCE_TARGETS.md
  • Design: docs/DESIGN.md
  • System tuning (sysctl / UDP buffers): docs/SYSTEM_TUNING.md — apply via sudo scripts/tune-system.sh apply

Using from another Zig project

This repo exports a module named quic. Consumers can import it via @import("quic").

  1. Add dependency (build.zig.zon)
.dependencies = .{
    // Use a pinned commit tarball
    .quic = .{
        .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/quic/-/archive/<commit>/quic-<commit>.tar.gz",
        .hash = "<sha256>",
    },
    // Or for local development
    // .quic = .{ .path = "../quic" },
};
  1. Wire the module (build.zig)
const quic_dep = b.dependency("quic", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
exe.root_module.addImport("quic", quic_dep.module("quic"));
  1. Use in code (src/main.zig)
const std = @import("std");
const quic = @import("quic");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();
    const alloc = gpa.allocator();

    var cfg = quic.QuicConfig{
        .alpn = &[_][]const u8{ "h3" },
        .enable_datagram = true,
        // Optional pacing and max datagram size
        .enable_pacing = false,
        .max_datagram_size = 1200,
    };
    const ep = try quic.endpointInit(&alloc, "0.0.0.0:0", &cfg);
    defer quic.endpointDeinit(ep);

    const conn = try quic.connect(ep, "127.0.0.1:4433", "test.local");
    defer _ = quic.closeConnection(conn, 0);

    // Drive IO & timers
    try quic.poll(ep, 10);
}

Notes:

  • Target Zig 0.15.1 for compatibility (ReleaseSafe recommended for production).
  • The module name is quic; no additional deps are required.

High-Level Transport API

For ease of use, this library includes a high-level transport layer that provides a simple, ergonomic API for building QUIC applications without dealing with low-level packet handling.

Features

  • Secure TLS Defaults: Explicit certificates required; optional self-signed generation for local testing
  • Connection Pooling: Manages multiple connections efficiently
  • Stream Management: Easy-to-use stream API with read/write helpers
  • Client & Server: Full support for both client and server sides

Quick Example

Using the transport module from a Zig project:

// Add to build.zig.zon dependencies
.quic = .{
    .url = "https://gitlab.com/devnw/zig/quic/-/archive/<commit>/quic-<commit>.tar.gz",
    .hash = "<sha256>",
},

// Wire the transport module in build.zig
const quic_dep = b.dependency("quic", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
exe.root_module.addImport("quic", quic_dep.module("transport"));

// Use in code
const transport = @import("quic");

// Server example
var quic_transport = try transport.QuicTransport.init(allocator, .{
    .port = 4433,
    .cert_path = "certs/server.crt",
    .key_path = "certs/server.key",
});
defer quic_transport.deinit();

try quic_transport.listen();
while (true) {
    try quic_transport.poll(10);
    const conn = quic_transport.accept() catch continue;
    // Handle connection...
}

// Client example
var client = transport.QuicClient.init(allocator);
defer client.deinit();

try client.connectEx("127.0.0.1", 4433, "certs/ca.crt", null, null);
const stream = try client.openStream(true);
defer stream.close();

try stream.writeAll("Hello, QUIC!");

Generate certificates with OpenSSL (or run ./create_test_certs.sh for local testing) and ensure cert_path, key_path, and ca point to the correct files.

Building Examples

Build and run the transport layer examples:

# Build examples
zig build examples

# Run server
# (Generate `certs/server.crt` and `certs/server.key` beforehand.)
./zig-out/bin/server-transport

# Run client (in another terminal)
./zig-out/bin/client-transport 127.0.0.1 4433 certs/ca.crt
# Or, for local testing only:
# ./zig-out/bin/client-transport 127.0.0.1 4433 --insecure

See docs/TRANSPORT_LAYER.md for complete API documentation and docs/GEODE_TRANSPORT_MIGRATION.md for migration from geode/bootstrap transport shims.

Process helpers

  • Update GAP after a slice: zig build tools && ./zig-out/bin/update-gap --summary "Finished <slice>"
  • Doc completeness check (CI gate): zig build tools && ./zig-out/bin/doccheck
  • Fuzzers build: zig build fuzz
  • Benches build: zig build bench && ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench [rtt_ns] [bdp_packets] [loss_every]

CC bench examples

  • Default: ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench
  • Single scenario: RTT=200us, BDP=100 packets, no loss: ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench 200000 100 0
  • Grid of scenarios: ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench --grid
  • CSV output (single): ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench 200000 100 0 --csv
  • CSV + grid: ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench --grid --csv (prints header and rows)
  • RTT=1ms, BDP=200 packets, drop every 50th pkt: ./zig-out/bin/quic-bench 1000000 200 50

CI

GitLab CI runs Zig build/test components, cross-language e2e interop smoke tests, security scans, SBOM generation/scanning, and semantic release automation. Quality and security tracking live in docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md and docs/QUALITY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md.

Observability

quic ships an optional OpenTelemetry seam that wraps each QUIC connection in a span. The seam is off by default and adds zero runtime overhead when disabled — every helper collapses to a comptime-known no-op and the otel dependency is never resolved (verified by otel/scripts/verify-consumer-noop.sh).

Enabling otel

zig build -Dwith_otel=true                  # build with otel linked in
zig build test -Dwith_otel=true             # run the seam smoke test

When enabled, application entry-point code (e.g. cmd/quic-server.zig) should bootstrap the providers once at process start:

const quic = @import("quic");

pub fn main() !void {
    var otel = try quic.observability_init.Otel.init(allocator, "my-service");
    defer otel.deinit();
    otel.installGlobals();

    // ... regular QUIC server / client code follows. Each `quic.connect`
    //     and `quic.accept` now opens a span; `quic.close` ends it.
}

Span shape

  • One span per connection ("QUIC connection client" / "QUIC connection server").
  • Attributes: network.protocol.name = "quic", network.transport = "udp", network.peer.address = "<ip>:<port>", plus quic.close_reason set on close.
  • Sampling default: parentbased_traceidratio @ 5% (override via OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER / OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG).
  • Exporter default: otlp/http/protobuf to http://localhost:4318 (override via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT etc.).

Stream-level spans are exposed in the seam (startStreamSpan) but not yet wired into openStream / acceptStream — high-volume call sites are deferred to a follow-up MR.

The full integration recipe lives in otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md.

Implementation Details

Code Architecture

  • src/quic/conn.zig: Connection state machine with full packet processing
  • src/quic/endpoint.zig: UDP socket management and event loop
  • src/quic/frame.zig: All 20+ frame types encode/decode
  • TLS 1.3: Provided by external tls dependency (see build.zig.zon)
  • src/quic/recovery.zig: Loss detection and congestion control

name: tls
description: QUIC-native TLS 1.3 implementation in Zig. RFC 8446/9001 compliant with zero external dependencies.
readme_content:
ztls

A TLS 1.3 implementation for QUIC written in Zig, strictly adhering to RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) and RFC 9001 (QUIC-TLS).

Status

Aspect Info
API Stability Production
Zig Version 0.16.0
Platforms Linux, macOS, Windows

Performance note

The <2 ms handshake target is validated on Ed25519 and RSA-2048 certificate configurations. secp256r1 (P-256) workloads currently run 2–3 ms per handshake due to an upstream Zig stdlib limitation (PERF-229). See ADR-0002 for the full decision record.

Features

✅ RFC Compliant - Implements TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446) and QUIC-TLS (RFC 9001) ✅ Zero Dependencies - Uses only Zig standard library ✅ Interop Tested - Conformance tests against BoringSSL and OpenSSL ✅ QUIC Native - Designed for QUIC integration, no traditional record layer ✅ Well Tested - 551 unit tests + RFC test vectors + 449 conformance tests

Quick Start

# Build and test everything
make

# Or manually
zig build
zig build test

Requirements

  • Zig 0.16.0 or compatible
  • OpenSSL development libraries (optional, for conformance tests)

Building

The project uses both a Makefile and build.zig for flexibility:

Using Make (Recommended)

# Build and run all tests (default)
make

# Build only
make build

# Run specific test suites
make test-unit           # Unit tests
make test-vectors        # RFC 8446/9001 test vectors
make test-conformance    # BoringSSL/OpenSSL conformance (requires libssl-dev)

# Development workflow
make dev                 # Format + check + unit tests
make clean               # Clean build artifacts
make help                # Show all available targets

Using zig build

# Build the library
zig build

# Run all tests
zig build test

# Run specific test suites
zig build test-vectors
zig build test-conformance  # Requires OpenSSL dev libraries

# With optimizations
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast

Test Results

Build Summary: All steps succeeded; 1000 tests passed ✅

Comprehensive Test Coverage:

  • 551 unit tests - Per-module tests with RFC subsection references (553 total, 2 skipped)
  • 449 conformance tests - BoringSSL and OpenSSL parity testing
    • Cryptographic operations (HKDF, AEAD, signatures)
    • X.509 certificate validation and chain building
    • Advanced X.509 extensions (OCSP, CRL, AIA, name constraints, policies)
    • TLS 1.3 protocol compliance (extensions, handshake flows)
    • Performance benchmarks (latency <2ms, memory <100KB)
    • Security testing (fuzzing, input validation)
    • Post-quantum algorithm readiness (parsing-only)

Total: 1000 tests ensuring RFC compliance, cryptographic parity, and production readiness

Project Structure

src/
├── lib.zig               # Main library entry point
├── tls13/                # TLS 1.3 handshake state machine (modularized)
├── tls13_full.zig        # Full TLS 1.3 message parsing
├── key_schedule.zig      # HKDF-based key derivation
├── record.zig            # Record layer & AEAD operations
├── x509.zig              # Certificate parsing & validation
├── sig.zig               # Signature verification
├── asn1.zig              # ASN.1 DER decoder
├── alert.zig             # TLS alert protocol
├── entropy.zig           # Fail-closed RNG helper (SEC-074)
├── zero_rtt.zig          # 0-RTT support
└── quic_*.zig            # QUIC integration interfaces

tests/
├── rfc8446_vectors.zig        # RFC test vectors
├── boringssl_conformance.zig  # BoringSSL parity tests
└── openssl_conformance.zig    # OpenSSL conformance tests

Usage Example

const std = @import("std");
const tls = @import("ztls");

pub fn main() !void {
    var gpa = std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator(.{}){};
    defer _ = gpa.deinit();

    // Configure TLS context
    const config = tls.Config{
        .allocator = gpa.allocator(),
        .role = .client,
        .supported_cipher_suites = &.{.TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256},
        .supported_groups = &.{.x25519},
        .alpn_protocols = &.{"h3"},
    };

    // Set up callbacks
    const callbacks = tls.Callbacks{
        .on_secret_available = mySecretCallback,
        .on_handshake_complete = myHandshakeCallback,
    };

    // Initialize TLS context
    var ctx = try tls.Context.init(config, callbacks);
    defer ctx.deinit();

    // Process incoming CRYPTO frames from QUIC
    try ctx.processCrypto(crypto_data);
}

Architecture

Design Principles

  1. INTEROP FIRST - Auto-detects and supports standard TLS 1.3 formats for compatibility with real-world QUIC implementations (quic-go, quinn, msquic)
  2. RFC-Driven Development - Every implementation block cites the relevant RFC section
  3. Zero External Dependencies - Uses only Zig stdlib primitives

Key Components

  • Key Schedule - HKDF-based key derivation using std.crypto.kdf.hkdf
  • AEAD Protection - AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305
  • Certificate Validation - X.509 parsing with SNI matching and validity checks
  • Signature Verification - ECDSA (P-256, P-384), RSA-PSS, Ed25519

Conformance Testing

The project includes comprehensive conformance tests to ensure compatibility with industry-standard TLS implementations:

BoringSSL Conformance

  • HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand parity
  • QUIC initial secret derivation (RFC 9001)
  • AEAD cipher compatibility
  • Alert code mapping

OpenSSL 3.x Conformance

  • EVP API compatibility
  • Cipher suite availability
  • Hash function parity
  • Key update procedures

To run conformance tests:

# Install OpenSSL development libraries first
make install-deps  # Auto-detects your OS

# Run conformance tests
make test-conformance

Observability

ztls ships with an opt-in OpenTelemetry seam. When the -Dwith_otel=true build flag is set, the library emits exactly one span per TLS handshake (span name: "TLS handshake") with the following semantic-convention attributes attached on completion:

  • tls.role -- "client" or "server"
  • tls.protocol.version -- "1.3" (always for ztls)
  • tls.cipher_suite -- the negotiated cipher (e.g. TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256)
  • network.protocol.name -- "tls"
# Default build: no otel symbols, zero overhead.
zig build test

# Enabled build: one span per handshake, exported via the OTLP
# defaults (http://localhost:4318) or whatever OTEL_* env vars
# specify.
zig build test -Dwith_otel=true

The seam is gated behind a lazy dependency, so the otel package is only fetched when the flag is on. Application entry-point code that wants to install a TracerProvider should call ztls.observability_init.Otel.init then installGlobals(); consult the upstream otel integration recipe (otel/docs/integration/RECIPE.md) for the full host-application bootstrap.

Documentation

  • BUILD_SYSTEM.md - Detailed build system documentation
  • CONFORMANCE_TESTS.md - BoringSSL/OpenSSL compatibility test documentation
  • CLAUDE.md - Project overview and AI assistance context
  • RFC References - All code includes RFC section citations

Development

# Quick development iteration
make dev

# Format code
make fmt
# or
zig fmt src/ tests/

# Check syntax
make check

# Clean build
make clean build

Implementation Status

✅ Completed

  • TLS 1.3 handshake state machine
  • HKDF key schedule (RFC 8446 §7, RFC 9001 §5.1)
  • AEAD record protection (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
  • X.509 certificate parsing and validation
  • Signature verification (ECDSA, RSA-PSS, Ed25519)
  • Alert protocol
  • 0-RTT anti-replay
  • QUIC integration interfaces

🚧 Future Work

  • HKDF-Expand-Label wrapper (tracked in test vectors)
  • OCSP stapling and SCT support
  • Full certificate chain validation
  • Additional cipher suites (AES-256-GCM-SHA384, AES-CCM)
  • Post-handshake authentication
  • Migration to stdlib X.509 when stable

Contributing

When adding features:

  1. Include unit tests in source files
  2. Add RFC section citations to all protocol logic
  3. Update integration tests if RFC compliance is affected
  4. Add conformance tests for cryptographic operations
  5. Update documentation

License

Apache-2.0 License - see LICENSE for details.

References

  • RFC 8446 - TLS 1.3
  • RFC 9001 - QUIC Transport TLS
  • RFC 9369 - QUIC Version 2
  • RFC 5280 - X.509 Certificates
  • RFC 7301 - ALPN

Built with Zig 0.16.0 | TLS 1.3 | QUIC-Native | RFC-Compliant

name: lieu-os
description: A hobby OS targeting IA-32 systems
readme_content:
Lieu is a hobby operating system primarily targeting IA-32 systems. The goal is to be able to run this on a PC I bought off Facebook Marketplace with 1GB of ram and an Intel Pentium 4 Northwood running at 2.66 GHZ. I might expand this to support other architectures, but at the moment I just want to reach user space for this target.

Why Zig?

I chose Zig as the primary implementation language for a myriad of reasons, namely its allocator API, build system, low level control, and additional safety. Generally, I would have chosen rust for a project that would benefit from safety such as this one, but when working with memory in the way that an OS needs to, I find Zig the better tool. Zig still has lots of safety checks and errors as values, which provide enough safety for me to fee comfortable using it.

The Zig standard library does not link against the C standard library, which allows much more of it to work without an OS. The same cannot be said for the Rust standard library aside from core and alloc.

Development

The easiest way to get started is to just run the Nix dev shell. Otherwise, you'll need the following packages:

  • Zig 0.15.1
  • Grub2
  • Xorrsio
  • Qemu (Optional, run with zig build run)
  • Bochs (Optional, run with zig build bochs)

name: reiter
description: Lazy, chainable and feature-packed iterators in Zig⚡
readme_content:
⚡reiter

reiter enables Ziglings to effortlessly create their own iterators for their favourite types. Iterators can be made for native Zig types, std/external library types or any other types.

This library takes inspiration and several ideas from the zig-iter library and Rust's std::iter::Iterator trait but does not promise to adhere 100% to any of their implementations.

Installing reiter

First, fetch the source using this command inside your Zig project:

zig fetch --save "https://gitlab.com/noahpolimon/reiter/-/archive/main/reiter-main.tar.gz?ref_type=heads"

Recommended for now

or:

zig fetch --save "https://gitlab.com/noahpolimon/reiter/-/archive/v0.6.0/reiter-v0.6.0.tar.gz"

Please note that reiter is currently not stable. You can replace "v0.6.0" with any version you want.

Then, add it in your build.zig file to the root module of your executable or library:

// code
+ const reiter = b.dependency("reiter", .{
+     .target = target,
+     .optimize = optimize,
+ }).module("reiter");

+ exe_mod.addImport("reiter", reiter);

const exe = b.addExecutable(.{
    .name = "my_project",
    .root_module = exe_mod,
});

b.installArtifact(exe);
// code

The last step is to run:

zig build

Voila! You may now import and use the reiter library.

"Implementing" Iter

Iter is a generic iterator that yields values from some kind of collection, range, indexable, etc... lazily. Iterators should have the following when "implementing" Iter:

  • Item - The Item declaration should be public and equal to the type of values the iterator yields.
  • fn next(*@This()) ?Item - The next method should be public and have the exact same signature.

A simple implementation would look like the example below:

// Import `Iter` from the lib
const Iter = @import("reiter").Iter;

// Create the iterator type
const MyIterator = struct {
    const Self = @This();

    // This is necessary so as to allow adapters such as Map, Filter, etc..
    // to obtain the type your iterator is yielding.
    pub const Item = u8;

    index: usize = 0,
    buffer: []const u8 = "wxyz",

    pub fn next(self: *Self) ?Item {
        if (self.index >= self.buffer.len)
            return null;

        const ret = self.buffer[self.index];
        self.index += 1;
        return ret;
    }

    // This is just an example. You may choose to use an `init` or `from`
    // method or any other way. However, any equivalent method/function to the
    // one below should return `Iter(@This())`.
    pub fn iter(self: Self) Iter(Self) {
        return .{ .wrapped = self };
    }
};

After creating an iterator it is possible to use and chain methods like so:

const my_iterator = MyIterator{};

var x = my_iterator.iter()
    .stepBy(1)
    .enumerate()
    .take(2)
    .map(u32, struct {
    fn call(i: struct { usize, u8 }) u32 {
        const j: u32 = @intCast(i.@"0");
        return j + i.@"1";
    }
}.call);

Apart from this minor detail :/

struct {
    fn call(i: struct { usize, u8 }) u32 {
        const j: u32 = @intCast(i.@"0");
        return j + i.@"1";
    }
}.call

Zig does not (and i think most likely will not) support closures. In the case it does in the future, this library will be updated to align with it.

See here to know which methods can be used on iterators.

Examples

More examples are found in the examples directory.

Initializers

Initializers are pre-made functions that can be used to create iterators for a particular Zig type or use case.

empty(type)

  • Creates an iterator that does not yield anything.

    var i = reiter.empty(u32);

_ = i.next(); // null

once(item)

  • Creates an iterator that yields item only once.

    var i = reiter.once(@as(u32, 50));

_ = i.next(); // 50
_ = i.next(); // null

onceWith(type, func)

  • Creates an iterator that yields the return value of func once.

    var i = reiter.onceWith(u32, struct {
    fn call() u32 {
        return 50;
    }
}.call);

_ = i.next(); // 50
_ = i.next(); // null

repeat(item)

  • Creates an iterator that yields item repeatedly. This is the equivalent of using once(item).cycle().

    var i = reiter.repeat(@as(u32, 50));

for (0..1_000_000) |_| {
    _ = i.next(); // always returns 50
}

repeatN(item, n)

  • Creates an iterator that yields item n times. This is the equivalent of using once(item).cycle().take(n).

    const n: usize = 3;
var i = reiter.repeatN(@as(u32, 50), n);

for (0..n) |_| {
    _ = i.next(); // 50
}

_ = i.next(); // null

repeatWith(type, func)

  • Creates an iterator that yields the return value of func repeatedly. This is the equivalent of using onceWith(type, func).cycle()

    var i = reiter.repeatWith(u32, struct {
    fn call() u32 {
        return 50;
    }
}.call);

for (0..1_000_000) |_| {
    _ = i.next(); // always returns 50
}

fromSlice(type, slice)

  • Creates an iterator that yields elements of a slice.

    const arr = [_]u32{ 0, 1, 2};
var i = reiter.fromSlice(u32, &arr);

_ = i.next(); // 0
_ = i.next(); // 1
_ = i.next(); // 2
_ = i.next(); // null

fromRange(start, end)

  • Creates an iterator from an integer range. The end value is exclusive.

    var i = reiter.fromRange(@as(u32, 0), 2);

_ = i.next(); // 0
_ = i.next(); // 1
_ = i.next(); // null

fromRangeStep(start, end, step)

  • Similar to fromRange(). However, the step can be modified. Negative step is possible as long as start > end, which is not possible with Iter.stepBy().

    var i = reiter.fromRangeStep(@as(u32, 0), 5, 2);

_ = i.next(); // 0
_ = i.next(); // 2
_ = i.next(); // 4
_ = i.next(); // null

recurse(init, func)

  • Computes the value of the next iteration from the last yielded value. init is yielded first then the next value is computed from it.

    var i = reiter.recurse(@as(u32, 0), struct {
    fn call(x: u32) ?u32 {
        if (x >= 5) return null;
        return x + 1;
    }
}.call);

_ = i.next(); // 0
_ = i.next(); // 1
_ = i.next(); // 2
_ = i.next(); // 3
_ = i.next(); // 4
_ = i.next(); // null

License

This project is licensed under MIT.

name: psql
description: Native PostgresQL client library with
readme_content:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

Migrated

new repo at codeberg

psql

A native PostgreSQL client for Zig, with many levels of abstraction

  • Connection: use .connect() and forget about it. a wrapper over Wire.
  • Wire: the PostgreSQL's tcp protocol implementation, accepts any reader/writer. a wrapper over Message
  • Message: the PostgreSQL messages' formats and parsers.

Installing

Compatible Zig Version: 0.15.1

  1. Add psql as a dependency in your build.zig.zon:
zig fetch git+https://gitlab.com/ouhamouy10/psql#dev-zig-stable
  1. In your build.zig add psql as a dependency you your program:
const psql_dep = b.dependency("psql", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
const psql_lib = psql_dep.module("psql");

exe_mod.addImport("psql", psql_lib);

EXAMPLE USAGE

a full example can be found in example and in connection's tests

Connecting

    var conn: Self = undefined;

    var reader_buffer: [14]u8 = undefined;
    var writer_buffer: [14]u8 = undefined;

    try conn.connect(
        allocator,
        .{
            .host = "127.0.0.1",
            .port = 5432,
            .user = "postgres",
            .database = "subhana_allah_pq_driver",
            .password = "bismi_allah",
        },
        &reader_buffer,
        &writer_buffer,
    );
    defer conn.deinit(allocator) catch {};

fetch All

    // v_varchar is VARCHAR in the db's table
    // we converted it to a .text type in the query
    // if we change 'v_varchar::text' to 'v_varchar'
    // we will then access it via `row.fields[2].varchar`
    var all_rows = try conn.fetchAll("SELECT id::int2, v_str::text, v_varchar::text, v_bool::bool FROM subhana_allah_t", allocator);
    defer all_rows.free(allocator);

    for (all_rows.rows) |row| {
        try stdout.print(
            "   {d}\t| '{s}' | '{s}' | {any}\n",
            .{
                row.fields[0].?.int2,
                row.fields[1].?.text,
                row.fields[2].?.text,
                row.fields[3].?.bool,
            },
        );
    }

querySimple + fetchRow + drain

PostgresQL sends one DataRow at a time. in psql you can fetch row by row, which might be useful for an allocation free query (for row)

    const descriptions = try conn.querySimple("SELECT * FROM " ++ table_name, allocator) orelse unreachable;
    defer {
        for (descriptions) |description| @constCast(&description).free(allocator);
        allocator.free(descriptions);
    }
    var fba_mem: [512]u8 = undefined;
    var fba = std.heap.FixedBufferAllocator.init(&fba_mem);
    const fba_allocator = fba.allocator();

    while (try conn.fetchRow(descriptions, allocator)) |*row| {
        defer {
            @constCast(row).free(allocator);
            // this is specefic to fba
            fba.reset();
        }

        // stream the row to a writer
        writer.writeInt(i32, row.fields[0].?.int4, .big);
    }
    try conn.drain(); // don't forget to drain

Extended query / prepared statements

    // pub fn prepare(self: *Self, name: []const u8, query_str: []const u8, param_types: []const ?PgValue.Type, allocator: std.mem.Allocator) !Wire.Statement
    var statement = try conn.prepare(
        "insert_rows_statement",
        \\INSERT INTO subhana_allah_t(v_str, v_varchar, v_bool)
        \\VALUES
        \\($1, $2, $3)
    ,
        &.{ .text, .varchar, .bool },
        allocator,
    );
    defer statement.free(allocator);

    for (0..20) |i| {
        try conn.bindExecute(
            &statement,
            "insert_rows_pr",
            Format.all_binary, // &.{ .binary }
            &.{ .{ .text = @constCast("subhana_allah")[0..] }, .{ .varchar = @constCast("alhamdo li Allah")[0..] }, .{ .bool = (i % 4 == 0) } },
            psql.Format.all_binary,
            allocator,
        );
        try conn.drain();
    }

executeExtended

    try conn.executeExtended(
        \\INSERT INTO subhana_allah_t
        \\VALUES
        \\($1, $2)
    , &.{ .{ .int4 = 2 }, .{ .text = @constCast("subhana-allah2")[0..] } }, &.{ .text, .binary }, allocator);

fetchAllExtended

just the result object is the same as that of fetchAll()

    var result = try conn.fetchAllExtended("SELECT * FROM " ++ table_name ++ " WHERE id > $1 LIMIT $2", &.{ .{ .int4 = 1 }, .{ .int4 = 3 } }, allocator);
    defer result.free(allocator);

zig build dev

Database Schema:

Web UI

  • Search for repositories in the main list
  • Provide numerical indicators for dependencies and dependants
